This is a great app and allows for complete control of your CPU.  There are some standard settings that you can use if you don't want to experiment, but if you really want control, you can set maximum CPU based on your battery level and for when your phones screen is off.  Some theorize that capping the CPU wont help since it will just cause your CPU to run longer and kill the battery anyway, but I disagree.  That may be the case on a rare basis, but overall it has really kept the usage under control.  To me, heat = major battery drain.  Since I installed this, I rarely feel serious warmth from my HTC HD2 (running froyo off SD card). On that note, you can also set up CPU temp profiles to keep it under a certain temp.  Best $2 I've spent so far!  Thanks!

I am an amateur, but am trying to get better at editing my photos (i.e. post processing). I recently purchased a [[ASIN:B005IHAIJ8 Sony NEX-5N]] and was using the Sony RAW converter (v4) for the first few weeks. While is does a pretty good job, I quickly realized that I would need a slightly more comprehensive editing package to get them where I ultimately wanted them and to remove imperfections and blemishes. It seems that PSP can make changes to a Sony RAW file, but it cannot save it back to ARW or even to RAW format (it saved an 'empty' file). You have to export it to JPG right then. Given this limitation, I will still be using Sony's RAW converter and use this for further editing. Furthermore, I think most photographers would recommend that you use the manufacturers RAW converter for best results.

The software is laid out well and I can quickly go from browsing photos to editing and back again. There are also many filters and effects that are easily applied with the click of a button. NIK Color Efex Pro 3.0 is really great with alot of filters that are adjustable. The filters in PSP are not adjustable, so the ability to tweak them in Efex is really nice. I have not found alot of use for FaceFilter Studio 2 as you can do much of the color and skin tone adjustments in PSP. This is supposed to allow you to tweak facial expressions, but it does not let you zoom into faces in order to place the markers. It basically needs to be a close up of someones face only to get them placed properly. Seems pointless. At any rate, the rest of the features are worth it to me.

I am running this on a laptop with Windows 8, a Core i5-3210M processor and 8 GB of ram and it does fine. You could get by with 4 GB from looking at my resources when editing. For the price (I paid $32 on a BF deal through Corel), this is a great value and I will get much use from it!

I have both previous Quells and love this puzzle style. I initially thought $2 was a little steep but im glad I bought it! I first thought the first few levels were too easy like the original, but later found out that I was supposed to find a gem on each level too, so I went back. Then I discovered secret levels, oh man!  And then hidden time pieces on the hidden levels, oh goody!  It engages you only like Quell can and they added enough to keep it fresh...  pick this one up!

I don't need a lot of bells and whistles that you might get with Photoshop. My primary need is to have the ability to use layers and to make selective edits. While X5 did those things, it was S-L-O-W (so much so that I stopped using it). Granted I am running this on a laptop, but I've got to work with what I've got. Its a newer laptop with an i5 processor and 8 gb of ram so its not bargain basement, but not top of the line either. The new X6 is noticeably quicker. It still takes a few minutes to load the program, but working on photos is much quicker.

For example, I sometimes stack photos varying the focal plane and then erase out of focus portions of other photos to end up with a sharp photo 'front to back' (AKA focus stacking or focus blending). In X5, erasing was extremely laggy... I would have to make a stroke and then wait a few seconds for it to actually happen. It was too laggy to be worth doing it. In X6, the edits happen as I do them (as they should), so now I will be able to implement this technique on more photos. Note that the photos I work on are TIF format, so they are large. You may not have issues in X5 working with compressed jpegs.

Another nice thing is that I recently purchased the NIK collection plugins for Lightroom and I was able to load them as plugins for PSP as well. One thing is you might have issues with Color Efex and Silver Efex, but there is a script you can download that will enable them to work. Google "Workaround for Nik Plugins on PSP X6" to find them.

All in all, the capabilities that you have with X6 is an extreme bang for the buck and was worth it for me to upgrade from X5 to X6 just so I will be able to use it more!

Note to new photographers: If you work with RAW files, you may still want to consider getting lightroom (student/teacher version is affordable... I know you have at least one teacher friend!) as it is much more streamlined for quickly working through your shoot and making basic edits. You can make your changes without having to convert all your RAW files. Then, for those few that need more advanced editing, you can launch PSP from LR by right clicking and selecting "edit in..." and selecting PSP (you have to set the path in preferences), which will convert your RAW to a TIF and open it in X6. You may also want to consider adding NIK (search internet for 15% off coupon code) for cool filter effects and stunning black and whites. There's your trifecta!

P.S. I did the download version and everything installed fine. I started with PSPX6 and then installed the plugins one at a time. Also, I'm running windows 8 and there were no issues there either.

I have owned this app since April when I purchased my Kindle Fire HD, and I have had no problems whatsoever. I have read a lot of negative reviews about this product, and all I can say is, either there is another app blocking its use, it's incompatible with a different app on the Kindle, or it's not compatible with certain versions of Kindle. As far as the grainy photos go, pictures are best taken where there is good lighting, either outside or a place in the home where there is plenty of light, but not too much, or you or your subject will look washed out. Now for the front-facing part: It takes practice to get good shots with this. I often find myself holding the camera off to the side so I can see what I'm aiming at. This works better than just aiming it straight ahead. So, if you find that your camera is stopping on you, there is something wrong in the Kindle itself, not the app. I would do a virus scan using Avast or another anti virus app to make sure, because as I said, this app has been great for me.

I thoroughly enjoyed this game and would like to see more like it. I started off playing Episode One and purchased Episode Two when it was released. Great story, not hard to control, and not impossible to beat. There's a lot of brain work here, but it's not too frustrating. You play as Joe Smith, a janitor who works at Archon Corporation. He suddenly becomes 'promoted' when his co-worker Frank goes missing. Later that day, he discovers a man from the future downstairs on the verge of death telling him that mankind will be extinct soon and that Joe needs to stop the process. The man gives him a portable handheld time machine and soon Joe's on his way to an incredible adventure. Find items, solve minor puzzles, and solve the mystery of mankind's demise. All in all, a game that gets you interested and keeps you there until the end. Well done by House On Fire!

This is a challenging game with truly gorgeous graphics and intriguing puzzles. As mentioned by other reviewers, try to avoid using the hints if you want to make the game last longer. Nothing is as hard as it seems-- just remember to look carefully at everything!!

EDITED TO ADD: Regarding game progress being lost-- use the menu and your back button to exit or the game won't save properly. Don't just exit using your home key.

I won't give away too much, but the ending felt unfair, as if I had just wasted all the time I spent solving puzzles and tracking down clues. That's the solution?? Why bother?? There is also a glaring plot problem that is never explained regarding Anna and her final action (it shouldn't even be possible).

That said, game play is fun, graphics are amazing, plot line is almost believable, so I still felt like I got my entertainment value. I do wish the map was interactive-- travelling back and forth got tedious. The built-in Guide is VERY thorough-- DON'T READ IT if you don't want spoilers.

One last caveat-- this is a serial murder mystery. As such, you are going to encounter LOTS of corpses. They aren't gory at all but they are intentionally startling, with each first appearance being extremely 'in your face' and accompanied by a scary loud crescendo in the music. I would probably rate this a PG13 if only for that reason.

Overall a very good game. I will definitely check out the sequel.

Storyline was a little lame (any child currently old enough to talk already knows that animal organs cannot be transplanted into humans in someone's basement). Puzzles were clever but glitches made them frustrating-- some click and drag solutions were so touchy that some puzzles could not be solved (solutions were obvious, but dragging one object onto the object you need to use it with had to be SO EXACT that the object continually snapped back to its original position). Puzzles whose functionality was obvious couldn't be played until the corresponding (unneeded) clue had been located. Lots of back and forth but that was less annoying than it could have been because the map IS interactive.

That said, the game kept me occupied over the weekend and was entertaining. If the glitches were fixed and some slightly more sophisticated game logic were employed I would have rated this five stars. Allow players to attempt discovered puzzles whether or not the 'clue' has been found. Make 'combination' objects less sensitive (if they overlap at all that ought to be good enough-- where is the logic in hitting one specific spike of a clustered crystal with the CENTER of a pickaxe? Shouldn't touching any part of the cluster with either TIP of the pick work?? And yet it doesn't...) Attempting to use objects 'out of story order' results in failure even though it is then REQUIRED that you go back and use them THE EXACT SAME WAY THAT FAILED THE FIRST TIME, because the story is farther along. If we can't attempt the puzzle yet, don't allow us to find/open them.

Don't misunderstand me; this is a well-constructed and clever game. It could just use some polish.

This is my first scrapbooking software. Unfortunately it did not live up to my expectations. For starters, the software has a few bugs and issues:

1. On "full Install" it tells you that you will need to use the 2nd CD (with the Art and Fonts) to finish installation, BUT it never asks for it. Installation completed with bare minimum artwork and the 2nd CD will not autorun in any computer I tried it on. It's very time consuming to try to find a graphic on the 2nd CD because there are too many folders!

2. The images are not "common" file names so you cannot import them to another program from the CD either. Basically - I can't use the artwork CD unless the CD is in the drive, which is not a possibility for me at all times, especially while listening to music.

3. Inserting New Pages - When the program starts it gives you the option to pick from a list of pages to use as templates for your first page. Unfortunately, once the first page is done you can't go back to pick from the templates for page 2. Your only options are to start a blank page, or duplicate the same page. This is a problem if you want one book with more than one type of page.

4. Cutesy artwork - the box that I purchased shows many examples of elegant looking scrapbook pages, but from what I can see of the artwork included, the templates are filled with cartoonish characters and designs. I was unable to find one template suitable for an adult birthday party, or adult get together. While there is a LOT of artwork, I would personally not use most of it.

If I were to say anything positive about this program, it's that it comes with many other features that it doesn't list on the box, such as a calendar maker, journal pages and label maker, etc. However I would have much rather skipped those "freebies" if it meant I got a higher quality product for what I want to use it for - no-nonsense scrapbooking. If my review was helpful please vote for it. Thank you for looking!

This month's free games are Teed Off (with talking Gopher reminiscent of movie Caddyshack), Rescue 911(where a Helicopter picks up your ball and moves it and then drops it), Big Hurt (which is a Baseball themed game) and El Doraldo (western theme).

Cat purring
crickets (I miss the crickets. We don't have them in Alaska.)
frogs
air conditioner (don't have those in Alaska either)
grandfather clock (too much like water dripping)
clothes dryer (gotta make sure the cats not in it)
chimes (okay)
oscillating fan (we use them in Alaska)
hair dryer blowing
dishwasher rinsing (comforting if the significant other puts them in it)
vacuum (I don't like to vacuum.)
airplane travel (I wish I were on leaving Alaska forever!)
cars driving (cars just passing by, no music blasting)
city streets (no shooting heard)
crowded room (ugh, it's stuffy in here.)
heartbeat (lub dub, lub dub)
Tibetan singing bowl (It bothered my hearing aids)
train ride (It rocked me to sleep.)
white, brown, pink, blue, violet noises (basically the same noise, didn't know noise comes in colors!)
Amazon jungle (birds were annoying to me)
beach waves crashing (ahhhhhh, I want to take the plane there.)
camp fire (I could almost feel the heat.)
ocean waves crashing (Wish I was listening to the plane on my way there.)
wind turbines blowing (nice and regular)
thunderstorms (I miss them. It was like being in the South again.)
rain on car roof (reminds me of rain on the tin roof in our house in the country)
rain storm (with thunder too!)
light rain (I danced in the rain as a kid. I'm 65 now and would like to do it again. Bucket list item?)
heavy rain (sounds like rain to me.)
extreme rain pouring (we don't get down pours much in Anchorage so kind of miss it.)
boat swaying in water (get me the dramamine please)
water dripping (absolutely hideous; whoever thought it was soothing needs their head examined)
water sprinkler (some of this water stuff is making me want to go to the bathroom!)
stream water flowing (pretty true to life)
running water (another bathroom call),
and I think that's it.

I'm only giving it three stars as there are pros and cons with this game:

Pros: It's a great game as it's like the old style RPG tactics games were back in the middle 90's - has a great learning curve to get started with the game and it gives you instructions on how to play, etc. Lining the formations up for strategic formations is pretty cool too - you can manipulate each character and move them where you want, but by doing that it uses up your AP points - movement to 1 square is 1 AP point - the AP points are limited to the characters. The play style is nice and the controls are pretty good - I used my stylus to move them to their squares. The graphics are way better than what was in the 90's and you can keep track of your player's stats, however.....

Cons: I usually play games on easy to get the feel of the game and see how it plays, then later I go back and play it on normal after I'm familiar with the game - putting this game on easy, seems easy at first, but as you go through just the first episode, it gets harder - you might as well be playing it on hard - the characters that are pre-loaded with the game seem really good at first, but once you get into about an 1-1/2 of play time, they are being over-run by enemies. The characters that are probably pretty awesome are the ones you have to buy. There's not enough potions in the first episode to even sustain your characters. You characters will die as there are more enemies than what they can handle.

There are waystations in the game that you can like take a break, but they do not fill up your magic points or health points. You have to rely on getting through hundreds of enemies with potions and what not and they are few and far between. The enemy has more moves than you do and they were able to go two rounds as I was only able to go one round.

I have never played a game like this that was suppose to be on easy and really it wasn't - the game would be better if there were more potions to be had in treasure chests to make it through the levels. Also you are able to get weapons and armor out of the chests, which I did, but you're not able to equip them on your characters. There's nothing like an inventory to go into to see what you have and to equip the characters with the treasure you have acquired. The only thing you can use are the potions.

I never made it out of the dungeons - I died 6 times just trying to get out of the place - the enemies are way more advanced then your characters and they have more hit points than you do.

Just so you know, I am a veteran video game player - I've been playing video games over almost 35 years - I own 3 video games systems and two hand helds - I have played many RPG games in my time, but nothing has been compared to this game - the game has potential to be awesome, but when the enemies are more advanced than your players, its not worth it to play the game if you can't keep them alive to beat the enemy. I have deleted this game off of my device and my cloud. I will just go back to playing Dungeons and Dragons Tactics on my psp. If the game could have been more like D&D, it would have been real fun to play - at least in D&D you can rest between battles and fill up your mp and hp. Too bad this game is not what it seems to be.

I downloaded this Screeble Pro app this morning as part of the Free App of the Day promotion. I like this app already because it does exactly what it's supposed to do. Keeps your Android phone or tablet on when holding it and allowing the screen to turn off when you put it down. I am testing this on my Samsung Vibrant and Nationite Midnite (Wits A81H+) and it works with out a problem. All you have to do is go into settings and check your preferences. Mainly you want to see what orientation range will Screebl recognize the phone or tablet is in use and should remain on. This works in both portrait and landscape mode.

The best thing about Screebl Pro is that as long as I hold it in my hand, my phone won't go off. I had my phone set at a long time so it wouldn't time out on me when I'm playing long games like Myth Defense. Now I have my phone set at 15 seconds, and it won't go off on me in the middle of a game.

There is also an indicator light at the top of the screen that lets me know if I'm holding my phone at an angle that will keep my phone on, just in case my hand drops too low.

I liked the promotion video and I don't see anything wrong with it. This makes the developer look more relaxed that some overactive actor on a typical infomercial. I like how creative Keyslabs was in marketing this product, while still covering all the main features. Screebl Pro is a very sensible product to use.

I hope Amazon Appstore continues to offer good apps like this as part of their promotion.

The smartphone UI is for a smaller screen, so there are few opt. I especially like the start page when you open the app on a tablet like the HTC Flyer. On left hand side it lists these options:

Recent files (browse you recently used files)
My Documents (your default document folder)
Local Files (files stored on memory card)
Ext SD (files stored on external storage)
Remote files (files stored on remote locations)
Download dictionaries (dictionaries to look up work meanings)

This is a great feature because it allows me an easier way to look up my files. I prefer to leave my documents on my SD card in case my device breaks, so I set my default document folder to one labeled "Files" on my SD card.

I recommend this app to anyone looking for a good mobile office app for their Android device.

When you destroy an enemy, it leaves coins behind that you have to tap or swipe to collect. I recommend this game to anyone who like TD games. Also this is a fun game you could let your younger kids play instead of something like GRave Defense.

Critter Escape is a well designed game. I got the game up as the Free App of the Day. Amazon lists this game as being a 48.9MB file to download. The graphics are the bright and fun. Playing this game is like watching a Saturday morning cartoon. There are two different play styles (line drawing style and virtual joystick style). I played for awhile on my Samsung Galaxy S2 using the line drawing style. I found it hard to be precise in dragging my finger across the screen. I'll try to test this out later on a 7" tablet to see if that helps. You may want to try using a stylus. I switched to virtual joystick style, and I found it easier to control my character. The good thing about this style is anywhere you touch on the screen, a virtual joystick appears, so this is works either right handed or left handed.

The main purpose of Critter Escape is to get your character out of the lab without being caught by a security guard. Your character was captured and brought to a lab to be a test subject. You can use stealth to move in areas of the screen where the guard can't see you. Or you can use powerups to become invisible like a ghost or bulk up for combat. Also you have little gem-like objects that you collect. You trace your finger around the screen. You draw your path and release to let him go. So you have to put a little planning on how you want to lead you character across the screen. The tutorial at the beginning is a must, so don't skip it.

However, I want to point out to anyone using a Android phone that this app is Wifi download only. So you can't download it on your phone unless you connect to Wifi either at home or at free Wifi spot.

I am writing this review after playing this game for one year in order to give the best review I can. I really enjoyed playing the game, the game has fantastic graphics, you don't need neighbors or friends to play, you can play off-line. You don't need to purchase crystals to play the game. Your charactor runs on energy, so every three minutes you get one more energy to use. You can also make more energy using the magic tent or potions table I think (it has been a while since I've played). The game has a story line and tasks to complete, some of them you need crystals, some of them you don't. You can gain crystals by finishing certain tasks, but you can also gain them buy buying certain animals with crystals (mainly dragons); but beware, one dragon eats crystals. I loved this game so much, I decided this game was worth purchasing crystals, so I did (almost $100 worth in a year).

The game it's self is great, which really deserves five stars; however, the developer, Game Garden, is NOT so great! I had a few problems along the way, purchasing crystals with special gifts not given; which I wrote the support about. I was not compensated, but the flaw was fixed. A year from the time I started playing Fairy Farm, the game just rebooted (re-started); started all over; however I didn't realize it was starting over, I thought I was beeing given a reward of being able to change my charactor with out paying chystals for it. NO, WRONG.... the game started over. I sent and email to support and told them about the problem, they told me they would fix it as long as I did not play the new game, well, it was too late. When I told them, I never heard back from them. I lost one whole year worth of progress and was lost in one day!!! I wrote several emails afterwards asking if they could just give me the crystals I lost back in one of their other games. Nothing, no response.

PS: Zynga Games are much better and their support, does support you!!1

I started playing two more Game Garden Games, and guess what? One of the games started all over again. I wonder if they will help me this time? I guess I'll have to see; on the upside, I did learn my lesson.... no more in game purchases!!! I have played a lot of games and this is the first developer that I have had no luck in getting a satisfactory answer or solution from them. So, there is my review, you can take it or leave it... but remember, if you have purchased in app items and your game re-boots (re-starts) on it's own, DO NOT play the game, get out and send an email to Fairy Farm support; hopefully they can help you!!!

When writing a review, I generally make a list of pros and cons. However, I am hard pressed to find anything negative to say about this app. As the name of the app would indicate, this is solitaire. If you have ever played solitaire, you should have an idea of what to expect. The layout and images are visually appealing. The touch screen controls are tight (very sensitive and responsive). Users can customize the rules to their liking. Cards and background can also be customized. The app is free, so it goes without saying that there are ads. Fortunately, these ads only displayed during the initial deal and then are gone for the rest of the game (occasionally, no ads at all). Shortly after I downloaded this game, I also downloaded FreeCell and Spider (Solitaire) from the same developer, MobilityWare. I recommend both as well.

Overall, this is a great game and a must download for solitaire fans.

Overall, Toto Fun is a very well executed app/game.  The pictures are very sharp and the touch detection is great. Also the menu system is very intuitive. If you haven't played the original Temple Run, the game is a "rail gesture" (my invented genre). This means the character runs forward on his own, and can do other actions via finger gestures (and tilting).

The overall gameplay hasn't changed from the original, which is only a minor disappointment. I wish the kept something similar to the archery component in Temple Run Brave, or a jump cancel (Subway Surfers).

The most noticable change is the enviroment. The graphics are more beautiful and there are a wider variety of obstacles. However, I consider this change more different than better. The original setting, while more simplistic, worked very well and felt more approriate given the title.

Another major change is the shape of the path. In the original, there the character moved in a straight line and made 90° turns. This time around, there are bends and hills. While these new geographical features reduce the monotony of the gameplay/surroundings, it also forces the player to react almost instantaneously when obstacles/icons "pop in" after moving around said features.

The biggest change in gameplay occurs during the mine cart sequenes. I loved the idea of this feature, but hated the execution. First of all, these sequences rely mostly on tilting. This would not be bad if the tilt recognition was calibrated better. Perhaps it's my device, but I had my Kindle completely sideways and still fell off of the rail. To make matters worse, the sharp/constant bends require you to react almost instantaneously.

Probably the most improved feature is the achievements and powers ups aspect of the game. Filling your meter and completing achievements actually help use/unlock items that are useful during the game. This is good for those of us that do not have an intrinsic value system.

Overall, you're getting a game with a much different look, but with an almost identical gameplay. While some of the new elements force the gamer to react on a whim (or die/miss an icon), others make accomplishing achievments more rewarding. I would recommend Temple Run 2 as a nice alternative to the original, but not as a replacement.

A lot of these reviews are very suspicious, and are most likely fake. With that being said, the game probably deserves a 3-star rating (or less). As far as comparing it to Temple Run, the overall product isn't nearly as good. The most obvious weakness is the scenery. Point blankly, the textures are dull. Furthermore, the frame rate is low. The character looks as if he's glitching, not running.

Despite it's flaws, it still has some impressive feature:
-variety of environments (as bland as they are)
-base jumping adds unique dimension to gamplay (needs polished)
-LOTS of power ups

Overall, the looks are underwhelming, but Survival Run still has some qualities that make it worth trying.

PeachTree accounting software was known for being dry, hard to use and more barebones than Quickbooks Pro. It sold decently well because it was nearly free to run year after year as long as you didn't mind inputting changes manually. That meant it was the go to for old school paper and calculator types. While the fancier, easy to use Quickbooks Pro was sold to the masses who wanted things more automated.

Enter the all new Peachtree for 2013--Sage 50. A lot more than just the name changed. The biggest change is that while more features are streamlined, many now cost extra like Payroll and updated tax tables. Removing the options for manually inputting updates, Sage 50 is now trying to target the Quickbooks Pro crowd. The problem is that this is very much still a work in process. It isn't as automated nor as easy to use as Quickbooks Pro yet. My feeling is that they should have moved into this market softer by charging for addons but keeping the cost much lower to get customers used to paying for such services.

They basically took the single "feature" from Quickbooks Pro that users complain about (random features that are required for almost everyone costing extra) and adopted it here. The problem is such changes likely to scare off current customers who used Peachtree for value (Think JCPennys recently) without bringing in new customers (because there is no real reason to select this over QuickBooks for most people).

So why three stars? Because it works if you don't mind paying for extra features and it is a decent sized leap over the Peachtree's of the past. Now if they keep improving it every year and maybe adjust what they charge for, I could see this finally stealing customers from QuickBooks in about 2-3 years.

If you are looking at using Ancestry dot com, then the 6 month included membership makes the Family Tree Maker software free as long as you don't want access to international records. The problem for me is that nearly EVERYONE comes from somewhere outside of the US at some point but those records are not part of the 6 month membership nor can you upgrade to those without paying a lot more.

To be even more clear, if this software came with a 6 month international membership (even if it was 50 percent more to reflect this addition) I would give it 5 stars. But while the software is great and sold, it is not worth the big price tag without the membership and the membership is limited because it is US only.

The software works like you would expect and never crashed on me. The value is decent if you need US only records but understand the included membership starts the day you install the software so wait to install it until you are ready to spend the time to fully use the service to get the most bang for your buck.

Pinnacle Studio 17 Ultimate has a lot going for it. The feature list is deep and diverse and when it works, it is a great program for the money. The problem is that it has a decent amount of bugs. Corel does continue to release updates but they have not made the product fully stable--esp for larger files.

If you read reviews you see many customers loving it and many customers hating it. I think the difference is that the folks loving it are working on simpler, shorter projects occasionally whereas the customers with lower ratings are more like me that attempt to use the program for more involved projects of 10+ minutes when the program starts to show its flaws.

So if your needs are simple, you will likely enjoy this. If you are looking to work on longer, more complex projects REGULARLY, you will likely be disappointed. Even with the most recent update it does still crash and not every feature fully works on every situation or source.

While I can say I recommend it, it is with that disclosure that I do so. If you are making your living with this, keep looking elsewhere.

As a life-long lover of video games, a game where I can control a game development company is ideal. This was the first Kairosoft game I played, and it made me fall in love with their products. It's cute, fun, fast-paced, customizable, and amazing. You get to choose what kind of video game to make, what system it's on, and train your staff to make the best game ever. Once again, Kairosoft Co has made a wonderful game. It mixes town building with monster fighting in an adorable way. You build your outpost so that adventurers will visit and then you help them fight the baddies around your town. The music is extraordinary in this one, especially during boss fights, I think; very dramatic. If you have played any of the previous Kairosoft Co games, this one will not disappoint. If you like simulation games where you build up a town, then you should get this. If you like games at all, this is the game for you!

Kairosoft, how I love thee. All of their games that I have been priveldged to play have been just phenomenal. Venture Towns, however, is a bit harder than some of the others. Yet, do not let that discourage you from playing this wonderful game. You have to build a thriving town for your citizens to work in. Not only that, bit you have to increase the price of your land, making each acre of property a pride for others to live near. The act of balancing finances, available jobs, roads, and your town's satisfaction will take you a while, but boy is it rewarding when you achieve it. I have played many games by Kairosoft and I whole-heartedly recommend this game to anyone.

I am a huge fan of Harvest Moon and Kairosoft, so this game is right up my alley. Yet again, Kairosoft has delivered a fantastic game! I really love the missions included. If you like sim games, casual games, or just all around fun games, I highly recommend checking this game out. I think this is the twelfth Kairosoft game I've purchased, and I have yet to be disappointed by their wonderful products!

This is a wonderful restaurant simulation game! Once again, Kairosoft made a wonderfully simple, yet super duper enjoyable game! Whether you've played other amazing Kairosoft games, or you're just discovering them, I highly recommend this game to everyone!

This might be my new favorite KairoSoft game. I really loved it! It combines the city building/management of Oh! Edo Towns and adds a very neat combat section of the game. The troop training and equipping are a nice twist to a city builder, I think. Not only do you have to maximize profits for your town, but you also are helping rebuild the Shogunate and fighting off evil samurai and bringing peace back to the country. I highly recommend this!

This might be the slowest-paced KairoSoft game I've played. I'm still unsure whether that's a good thing or a bad thing. It's cute and easy going. The horses are adorable. I like this game, but probably not my absolute favorite KairoSoft game, but still a wonderful game!

Corel Fusion ... I bought it as an early release last year, and today, Corel still sells only version 1.0.0. No updates are available. Will they ever? Does it need updates? My answer is most certainly, but until then, it has its useful side.

What I use it for:
...1. Expanding or combining documents -- not just pdfs, but office suite products such as from Microsoft or a version of Open Office - it claims over 100 supported filetypes. It probably does, but maybe it will not support all the features of each orginally created product. Examples under Cautions, below. Don't assume they are comprehensive.
...2. Rearranging PDFs -- for instance -- I put together several documents to be sent as a single fax while retaining a digital copy. When I have several audiences, its easy in assembly mode to rearrange pages for different emphasis, delete unneeded pages, add new ones in a single package, regardless of original and mixed formats that may be present.

What I wish I could do:
...1. Add password / encryption.
...2. Edit documents directly: (its possible to make simple substitutions, such as correct spelling from "to" to "two" for example, but) its not possible to replace sentences across multiple lines in one simple step.

Cautions:
If you have a PDF form which allows you to save data in fields, and you have done so with another product, DON'T use that file with Fusion. When I save such a file with this product, the field data is omitted and deleted (even from view in real-time)!

If you embed graphics in a Word type document, keep a backup. This product may mis-render some of the colors.

The document has not printed all my PDFs clearly. For instance, I had a form with 3% of the text oriented vertically along an edge; and I've had otherwise normal text with phrases bolded. In both cases part of the text on those lines printed too faint to read. They printed fine, in the main competitor's product.

Quirky Registration: Watch your order fulfillment documentation carefully -- look for a serial number in the format of XXXX-XXXX- etc. Entering it into the program will take you out of trial mode. The quirky part is if you try to register via the website, it will hand you a confirmation code not at all like the SN and doesn't work for the program's activation prompt.

Shame on the manufacturer for making zero fixes since April 2011. Other reasons for downgrading it are (1) sometimes possible to lose content or (2) have graphics altered. For simple text documents it works fine, but if you create tables, insert graphics, use outlines, change fonts or styles, test out the trial version thoroughtly before making a decision.

Printing with this plug-in is from within the application if it was written using Amazon's specifications. Asuming that's true, then follow the below steps, borrowed and modified from a January reviewer.

1. Let's assume you are within your app such as Amazon's Silk, or email interface.
2. Keep in mind this app prints let's you specify pages, but not selections from within a page.
3. At the top right of the screen, tap on the three vertical dots. You may need to switch to landscape mode in order to see the dots. This should display a menu with "Print" being one of the options.
4. Tap "Print". This should bring up a list of detected printers on your network of which there may only be one unless you have other supported printers on the same network.
5. Tap your printer.
6. Another screen should appear showing the printer name and its status (ex. - "Ready"), the number of copies to be printed, and a "More options" set (this lets you select the paper size , for example). And below that will be a "Print" button.
7. Carefully review all options and change them as necessary.
8. Tap the "Print" button

Keep in mind there is no access to the print queue from the app. E.g. you can only cancel the job from the printer.

WISHES: 1. A way to save selected options, eg papertray, color/b&w...
2. More options: Select dual sided printing; fast or standard;..

Thanks Canon for what's here so far.

If you have a recurring use from a particular source, the first time you find that source on Boxcast, be sure to indicate it as a "favorite". From that point on, you'll be able to avoid protracted searches. Here's what I suggest for those unfamiliar.

The first time the app came up, a spinning box continued indefinitely. Rebooting my Firestick fixed that. Subsequent times, it is best to wait until the spinning box stops, and a faint count of available sources is listed on the screen. If you have a favorite, move the cursor down to that spot, skip History, and select the favorite of your choice. It will appear on the screen. Move the cursor right and select that particular favorite, even if it is the only one. You'll then be shown a list of what's available from that source, The latest should be on the left edge, but you may have to wait for a few seconds before the list is updated. To me, in the world of Android grocery lists, there are two major players. There's a few more, but I really don't feel like the android version of grocery king or OI shopping list stand up to these two. So that leaves you with Grocery IQ and Mighty Grocery. While both are target the same audience. And Grocery IQ is free, mighty grocery does have a lot of features, enough that the $3 could very well be justified.

Grocery IQ:
When I started using this, I had a lot of sync issues which turned me off of this. But I recently tried it again, and the sync worked this time around. It's simplified, compared to mighty grocery. Quick lists, easy ui, can share lists between say you and your wifes/husbands phone. Does a pretty good job organizing, ok barcode scanning, and can email list to yourself. Overall, for free, it's extremely useable, and worth the download. The only thing that really annoyed me are the coupons, uses coupons.com service, which makes you jump through a lot of hoops to actually get a coupon printed out.

Mighty Grocery
I was actually pretty satisfied using the free version of mighty grocery, until amazon decided to give the full version away. Even the free version does a great job of auto-categorizing the foods you enter. And it goes well beyond just that, letting you customize the aisles/categories and predefining food to go into which. If you're motivated, you can really strategize the hell out of your shopping trip. Full version adds things like recipes, extends predefined lists, backup, barcode scan, configurable tabs, and screen rotation. Which a few of those actually come in pretty handy. Because of the amount of features, certain areas of mighty grocery definitely take some time getting used to. UI is good for what it is, but you definitely can find yourself getting lost. Having so many options with things like predefined catalogs, recipes, and so many options to share, are the real selling points to me. I can dump lists to facebook, springpad, my email, dropbox, etc. And starting with my previous list is essential for my shopping needs.

Winner? To me, they are both great applications, and grocery IQ being free makes it totally worthwile. But for me, i still love mighty grocery. It's worth the $3. After I took the time to get used to it, i can't go to anything else. Try the free version, compare yourself.

VS OTHER TOWER DEFENSE GAMES:
There are a ton of tower defense games for android, a lot of them are fantastic. So which should you buy? Heres a list of the ones that i've played:

Robo Defense($2.99): Awesome game, does eventually get old, but completely worth playing.
Hex Defense($1.49): Clean, smooth, definitely fun.
GRave Defense HD ($.99 on sale): additional survival mode gives a ton of extra play time, updated graphics, and overall great look and feel make this a steal.
Crystallight Defense ($2.95): Interesting wep upgrades, and challenging levels, decent game overall.
Retro Defense ($4.99): One of the oldest td games for android, simple and clean. Very straightforward, lot of maps. It'll last awhile and is a lot of fun.
defensoid($.99): Similar to retro defense.
Guns'n'glory($.99): Interesting twist on a TD, allowing units to be moved around, lot of maps.

Honestly, out of this list, robo defense and grave defense are my favorites. Retro is awesome, but it's not really updated anymore and it's no longer worth the $5 in my opinion. Hex defense is clean, follows a similar vein to retro defense, and is a better value for the money. Robo defense was addicting, but I ended up playing the same level over and over and the novelty eventually did wear off.

Guns'n'glory is great game by itself but stacked up against the competion, if you had to buy just one, i'd buy grave defense HD...It has some of the best graphics in a tower defense, plays smoothly, is currently on sale, and lasted the longest keeping my interest.

I gave it one star less because of the privacy concerns.  I would not install it on a phone where I keep real private information. I don't think my tv programming viewing patterns are that interesting :)  But I certainly would not install it on a cell or tablet where I might save more personal information.

I find this process killer really helps me keep Kodi's performance in good condition.  Unlike some other Android set-top boxes that have a built-in way to see what other processes are running in the background, Amazon's version of Android on their FireTV devices does not.  Unused apps in the background occupy the little amount of precious RAM memory from your foreground tasks.  In the case of Kodi that benefits from additional ram to establish a streaming buffer, the less ram it has, the more video buffering is likely to occur.  Before running Kodi, run this app and close any unneeded apps that are still in memory.  This will provide Kodi with the maximum amount of memory to use for a memory buffer.

The app is extremely limited compared to the website, however.  You do get significantly for information on their website.  But this app has most of the major streaming providers at a touch of your remote control.  Hopefully, they keep developing the app so it matches the amount of information the website provides. This is a really great game. So far I have not spent a penny on this game and I have been playing non-stop.
This is a build-it kind of game unlike any I have played so far. The tutorial at the beginning is short but good. After I was on my own I still get certain things I must accomplish in order to get coins and level up.
So what's so different? Well you build your world from the cells on up, kind of. For instance: pretty much all your playground is water, you place rock or dirt or sand into the water and begin to create your land onto which you will build a primitive wood lean-to for my first human to live.
Mixing the "ingredients" you are provided with you create new ones. So: sand on water=desert, add grass and you get a cactus, now add grass again and you created a Palm tree.
You build your land, detail it, build housing from primitive on up, make a tree, build a lumber shack, get a human (random) to work the mill, cutting down the trees. You grow bushes and he cuts them to kindling. Of course you also have a farm with a worker who gathered the grass you provided to feed the sheep and cuts up the meat for sale to the market and individuals.
You get to build a market where individuals are selling your goods. The coins from the sales will be used to build more and upgrade.
While you wait for the wood to be cut and processed you learn to create land, a volcano, mountains, swamp, flowers, an inventory which is ever expanding by mixing items together into new items, items you created, into an ever expanding inventory.

I can sit down with this game and suddenly it's 3 hours later without me noticing time has moved on while my world is expanding according to my own imagination and ideas.
This creativity is what has so endeared me to this game. It's not - what the game developers want this world to look like, not by prior design - but entirely how I want it, how I dream it up. My Kindle is a 1st gen, and won't run this game, so my play time is based off of my Acer Iconia.

First, the game play. It's Vice City, period. :) I haven't found anything missing from it so far, as it includes the opening, cinemas, missions, and everything originally found on the PS2 version. To find out more about that, I recommend searching Google or a game site such as IGN or GameSpot for a review. If you know GTA, which you likely do if you're reading this, then you'll find it all here for $5. :)

The graphics are not up to today's console standards, nor some Android games... But they are much better than the original PS2! :) Considering this is an open world game on a phone/tablet, it's quite good. Lighting and effects are much improved over the PS2, making it look great. The sound is surprising, as it seems to have the full 80's soundtrack, and all the other voice and effects the original had. On the Iconia, the graphics are silky smooth and no glitches whatsoever.

Controls! The sticking point in any game like this on a touch screen... Not bad at all! Controlling your character is a virtual d-pad that appears wherever you touch on the left, and is analog. Controlling your car is a touchier subject, as default controls are digital and tend to cause you to over-steer a lot. In the options, however, you can activate tilting your device to steer, as well as turning on analog steering. I've never been much for tilt steering, but the analog suits me just fine. You are also able to customize the location and size of all the game's controls. So far, I'm liking how the default works.

I recommend checking the supported devices first to make sure yours is on the list, and if you plan to run it on the Kindle Fire, make sure your firmware is up to date.

All in all, an excellent port of a game I loved 10 years ago, and still even own. :) If you like the violent sarcastic world of Grand Theft Auto, remember this game fondly or want to know what all the talk was about, $5 is a very worthwhile price!

I bought The Room and loved it so much that I had to get The Room Two. The game has beautiful graphics and the puzzles are incredible. But it is an addictive game. Since I got both games within days and played them for a few hours once I was done, I was dreaming about solving the puzzles.

If I were to say it has one weakness, it would be that the game (both games) are too short.

I was a little bored. It didn't have hints and I spent a lot of time trying to figure out if there was a clue to help me I deleted it almost immediately. Having played far superior games: The Room and The Room Two, I may try to tackle this game again. If I do and determine that there is something that I missed the first go round, I'll re-review. But at this point, I'm sticking with the fact that there isn't that initial thing "out of place" that focuses the player.

This game is so addictive that it's impossible to believe. There would be times when I would sit in my car--home from work--playing the game to "get just one more clue then I'm going inside." And when I get that one more clue I couldn't put it down. The strength of the game is that it's fun and tells a little story. But there are a couple of weaknesses.

1. When you tap on the map, you see where you are an where the next actionable place is. What I would have liked is that I could tap on the next actionable place and be whisked to that place. Instead, I close the map back out of where I'm at, back out of the next place, back out of the next place. It's like driving and going past your stop but you can't make a U turn. I was annoyed by that; especially since the game was so addictive that I would play late into the night so I was sleepy and not functioning so I would get lost and have to tap the map to figure out where I am to try to get to my destination.

2. Sometimes to get a mini-game or function to work you had to be very precise in where you placed a found object. There were times that I didn't think that the item was to be used in a place because I would drag it to the place and it would fall back into inventory, drag it to a new place, fall back into inventory. One time I dragged and hovered and released and it fell back into inventory. Since this was a very specific piece I knew that it belonged there. I went to another actionable place and returned later, doing the same thing but the second go round it eventually took.

3. A request to rate the item would pop up while you were playing. This was annoying since I didn't think rating was "mandatory" for a game that I purchased. But the request to rate popped up while I was in the middle of a mini-game and when I clicked the X button to get out of the rating request, it reset my mini-game. I was peeved because I was close to solving that game and it reset to the very beginning.

4. When I finally won--finished. It didn't do a "congratulations" celebratory thing for me. Sure I released some souls but the next thing I knew, I think I was being taken back to the room where I started. So I didn't get the "in your face" celebration.

5. In addition to mini games, there are side items to find. I found I believe 22 of 42. You would think that after I won, I would have been allowed to go back to look for those other items but I wasn't, what with me being whisked back into the asylum.

While I listed those small items as weaknesses, the overall strength of the game makes it something that I would recommend to others if you like solving puzzles. And if "part 2" comes, I'll definitely get it.

The gist of this puzzle game is that you feel around and touch every thing in the room to find out what is a useful object and what is not. Then you touch objects in the found object bar to see if those objects are to be used together. The puzzle is not intuitive and there are no hints so you're basically feeling until you stumble on the right thing and the right got get out of a room. In addition, if you're in the middle of a room, you can't save your progress. I'm stuck in one of the rooms and when I log out and log back in, I have to start over with collecting the items. I've deleted the puzzle and kept it on my cloud but I'm not sure if I'll return to it.

I could listen to the narrator talk all day and the music is ok. I'd give 6 stars if there were more villages or larger areas to develop. This game is well-done and engaging. Love it for free, would buy it for $2.99. Good for anyone who enjoys mythology and has patience for matching games & village building.

I'd never seen a logic game quite like this before. I got this as the FAOTD for my 1st gen KF. This kept my interest for a number of levels. Different types of creatures have their own set of rules that force you to keep changing strategy. The board setup for each level changes things up further. This is excellent for young players, but small children may not have much fun with the more advanced levels. There is a timed hint option that shows you the solution one move at a time, so you can't flip straight through to the solution as quickly. Personally, I think the $2.99 is high, but this type of game isn't my favorite. It does have a lot of levels. I wasn't clear on the permissions, but it was ad-free and I didn't see any IAP. Overall, it seems a strong effort.

TurboTax makes tax preparation much less drudgery, assures mathematical accuracy, and last-minute revisions (eg. incorporating more deductions) a breeze.  Also provides good help and suggestions.  A bit pricey, though.

I've had mine for about 9 months - lately has frozen up. Will not sweep, update, or even display alerts. Efforts to obtain techical support directed me to re-install - hopefully it works, though you never know if it's really working until it doesn't

H&R Block wanted $300 for a simple personal income tax with 1099s, trying it manually left me with forms all over the table and floor, and erasing holes into the papers. Eventually Turbo-tax Home/Business did the job, but not before considerable aggravation.

Specifically, I wanted to enter mileage for job searches, and the program wouldn't let me. Tried phoning for help, and was notified there was a 45-minute wait-time; alternative was to appeal to a users' group. (No offense intended, but the idea of asking others who may or may not be knowledgeable seems like Turbo-Tax is pawning off their responsibilities to help users to others.) Finally ended up stuffing the mileage into another area - hope I don't get audited. On the plus side, really appreciated TurboTax's ability to immediately make revisions (including on state tax forms), and the ability to e-file the federal forms.

Finally, charging extra to e-file state forms just seems like unjustified chiseling.

The good news is that the upgrade did a good job - my former programs and settings were exactly as before. The disappointment is that I still couldn't view videos (problems with Vista before), and couldn't download new Windows Photo Gallery viewer (have almost 8,000 photos). Very aggravating - hence, my initial one star rating.

Then, wife was able to view videos (I still can't), and Wondows Photo Gallery viewer miraculously appeared. I guess the key here is patience. Hoping I'll be able to view videos soon. If not, it's still better than Vista. Other problems continued from Vista include creating about 80 registry problems and incredibly overloaded temporary files whenever I shut it off - mostly I just put it to sleep when leaving, except for updates.

After an hour or so, I gave up and went to Fry's Electronics site - paid $54 there, with $50 in rebates. However, if I'd seen this price first I would have certainly taken it. The 'good news' is that installation was easy, though took several minutes. Also was intrigued by the new feature that checks one's 'Facebook Wall' to see if anything potentially dangerous is there. Two days later, tried again. Finally got someone at Microsoft that knows what he's doing. Said I should switch to Google Chrome, did so, and it downloaded immediately. Now I need to learn how to use the new, hopefully improved, Word 2013 - I should have ordered the assistance guide that was offered in accompaniment - have now done so.

I upgraded to Windows 8 because my Windows 7, which I generally liked, was repeatedly breaking down, possibly because of innumerable updates over the years. Windows 8 offered a brand new start and purported to also provide security enhancements. Since someone had also invaded my Hotmail account and was using it to send marketing pitches to others, I thought Windows would solve all my problems. Instead, it brought innumerable new headaches and frustrations, thanks to its confusing and difficult to learn interface . (I greatly prefer use of a keyboard and mouse instead of a touchscreen.)

Using Windows 8 is akin to decades-ago games such as Super Mario where one was constantly hunting for hidden coins or secret passages; in Windows 8 those coins/secret passages provide the means to access important screens and options. Unfortunately, they don't reliably appear even when one knows exactly where they're hidden. On the plus side, it is now easier to rid one's computer of Bing and replace it with Google, once and for all. Another negative, while hardly important, is that the new Solitaire is less user-friendly than the one that came with Windows 7.

The really good news is that I soon learned about Windows 8.1 - a much simpler and intuitive version that allows those used to desktop procedures to make use of their computers again without having to constantly refer to a 'How to' book.

My 12 month subscription was about expired on Norton Internet Security 2011 so I was going to buy from Amazon the same product to extend my subscription (yes, it's cheaper to do it this way vs. ordering directly from Symantec). I found that Norton 360 version 5.0 (contains NIS 2011) was about the same price at the time from Amazon so I decided to "upgrade" to Norton 360 from Norton Internet Security.

I had no problems installing / updating to this version on both my PCs, one running Windows XP Professional and the other Windows Vista. As with any software, make sure your system meets the minimum system requirements before buying and attempting installation. Make sure you have an internet connection and have your Norton User Name & Password handy (if you're an existing Norton customer).

One thing I'd like to point out that is important, if you have any remaining subscription time on NIS and choose to upgrade to Norton 360 YOU WILL loose your remaining time left on NIS.... SO WAIT TO INSTALL. This made sense and I'm not complaining but just be aware this will happen. I lost about a week's worth the subscription time but anticipated this issue. If you install the SAME product for renewal, your remaining subscription time IS added to the new subscription. Makes sense.

I found Norton 360 had a few nice features NIS did not, especially disk and registry clean up... and used them as soon as it was installed. I was surprised at how much "garbage" was left behind from uninstalled apps and temporary files (Windows files not Internet). I don't think I'll use the online backup feature but you may find it handy.

Final thoughts, if Norton releases a new version of this software during your subscription time, you will be eligible for that product update (not just Norton Live Update software patches and virus definition updates). So don't be concerned if you're expiration is nearing and you're already using the current version being sold. What you're buying is a subscription, not a particular version. I've been a Symantec / Norton user for over 15 years.

This could be a good game, but the constant attempts to make players purchase "game currency" and in-game items ruins it. Advancing in the game requires various items, but they're almost impossible to find so you're forced to search the same locations over and over, sometimes under extremely difficult conditions such as complete darkness but for one small lighted area. Of course you can use "tools" that you purchase, and again, it's constant badgering to buy, buy, buy. Finding the required number of objects within the allotted time is very difficult even under ideal conditions. Again, you can extend the time limit by purchasing tools. For me, a game should be relaxing, but with Hidden City, the time limitations leave me feeling pressured and frustrated. I refuse to spend any money to purchase game items which makes it impossible for me to advance. I have a "collection" to assemble but was missing one item required for assembly. I was constantly hounded to 'Buy Now!" -- which I didn't do. Instead I spent days searching the locations and either failing to finish the task (thereby losing any found items) or failing to find the necessary object. Even unlocking a new area requires payment -- through crystals or gold collected -- with the obvious intent of making you use what you've earned in the game so you'll buy more. It's a shame. This could be a very good game.

I will say that this game is better than a lot of other games I've played, but it's still filled with frustrations. I am unable to log in to connect with Facebook so I am missing out on many bonuses. Funny thing, though, when the game asked me to LIKE the developer's Facebook page, it connected right away. Finding support is difficult, and I doubt that I will get much help if and when I do manage to contact them. Games like this could have a much larger and happier customer base if G5 wasn't constantly badgering players to buy game tokens and making the game almost impossible to advance in without paying. I have not and will not spend money for any in-game purchases. I would much rather fail at a game than to reward the developer's overwhelming greed.

I'd like to give this game a higher rating, but the slow pace makes it difficult for me to recommend it. While it could be a valuable educational game for children, it quickly gets frustrating because of the slowness. When asked, for example, to make a four-letter word from the letters O P S T, there are many choices but only one correct answer. Having to slowly enter over and over really spoils any enjoyment, plus the "brain" screens between each puzzle slow things down even more. For adults, it's too boring. I feel compelled to contradict some of the other reviewers here. This is not a bad upgrade at all, it just depends what you expect for your money.

I installed Q Premier 07 over Premier 06. It installed with no problems (Win XP Home), converted my two files without any hitches or data errors, and works quite effectively. I should mention here that one of the files is large, and has a lot of complicated investment history -- it has sometimes caused problems with earlier versions of Quicken.

I tend to upgrade most years, simply to get the latest bug fixes, tax rates, etc. And as others have noted, Quicken has mostly confined itself to relatively minor improvements, and you could certainly say that the story remains the same here. If you don't like spending the money, and are happy with your 05 or 06 version, don't bother. But if you're considering upgrading for whatever reason, don't be scared away, jump in, the water's fine. The downloads are definitely better, and a tad faster (Q seems to be able to run some downloads in parallel now).

I haven't explored all the other "new" features they claim, but so far the good news is that nothing I depended on is broken.

UPDATE 1/24/09:

I am still very satisfied with this product. So far I've entered all my data, and it's been pretty painless, both for Fed & State taxes.

I have to qualify this by saying that my taxes are pretty simple this year, with no AMT, no sch C, no sch K, etc. So I'm not really running into some areas that are often not handled well in tax software.

One thing I liked better than turbo tax was the simpler handling of tax-exempt income, splitting the in-state vs. out-of-state portions. Also, similarly, the handling of US Treasury interest (tax-exempt for state tax). Turbo Tax makes you enter separate 1099s for each part, instead of just capturing the information within one form dialog.

On the other side, I have some additional critiques:
(1) no ability to import/download W2 & 1099 data (not that I found, anyway)
(2) form 1116 has to be filled out manually, even if it's pretty straightforward -- they could have and should have provided an interview for this
(3) no way provided to simply delete a line in a form (minor point, turbo tax has this, and I find it very useful) -- you can of course delete the data in the line

INITIAL REPORT:

Obviously, it's a bit too early to provide a thorough review of the program, because it's essentially incomplete (as is TurboTax): many tax forms are still not available in their final form. There will be a Dec 11 update, and I expect several others over the next couple of months. (I've learned from past experience not to submit final returns until late March, since the bug fixes and form corrections are often not final until then. This is true for either TurboTax or TaxCut.)

However, here's my current take: this is a fine program, and certainly more than adequate for the necessary help preparing a tax return. I've used TaxCut in the past, but have used TurboTax for the past few years. I decided to use TaxCut this year because of the price difference, and because the new licensing policy for TT is annoying. So far I'm finding it easy to use, and trouble-free in importing data from the previous year TurboTax file and current year TXF files.

One minor weakness compared to TurboTax: I remember that in the 07 TT you could remove a specific set of imported data; I haven't found anything like that in this program. Not a biggie for me, since I always save "checkpoints" in separate files so I can revert to a previous version if I need to, but it's the kind of little thing that makes TT a bit better in my opinion. Just not sufficiently better that I will pay anything Intuit wants to charge (just a matter of principle for me).

Some general comments, based on experience over many years of doing my own (often very complicated) returns: Neither program is perfect by any means. For many complicated situations you have to do your own calculations externally (I use Excel), or enter data manually. Be aware that dealing with AMT, AMT credits, and stuff like that remains mind-bendingly difficult, just not as nightmarish as doing them without a program to help. And you should always sanity check your results, because odd calculation bugs can persist for a long time. (I found a very stupid, but hard to find, calculation bug in TurboTax a few years ago, having to do with AMT.)

I will post an update in a few weeks when I've had the chance to make more progress with my return. Will be able to review the state program as well at that point, perhaps.

Rosetta Stone programs are very good for a quick and fast intro to a language, especially for the casual visitor. I used a previous version to help me learn enough French to get by on my frequent visits to Paris (on business), and my son has been using this version to support his school French classes. I found it very helpful in getting me quickly to a point of learning basic (broken) French, and improving my pronunciation and accent. My son has had similar experience.

But be wary of the company's hype, that this is equivalent to an "immersion" program for learning a language, etc. That's nonsense; in fact, I found it very lacking in helping understand French grammar, and completely inadequate sometimes in just helping understand French words.

So use it by all means. But a good French-English dictionary is essential. And so are friends/teachers who know the language and culture: I found it very necessary to ask questions of my French colleagues about proper idiomatic (and cultural) uses of various words and phrases.

I'm neither a Quicken-hater nor a raving fan. I use it because it helps me manage my financial life, and I haven't found anything better ... yet. It mostly works.

This is a review based on first impressions after a recent upgrade; I will update if I have further information to share.

Review begins here ...

As the world knows, Quicken hasn't really improved much over the last 5 years or so -- they just go through with UI changes and minor tweaks. And the changes usually fall equally between "annoying, why did they change that?" and "ok, maybe that's a slight improvement".

I just upgraded from Q2007, and only because of the "current + 2 previous" support policy. (No, I don't have a big problem with this policy.)

The upgrade was painless, and the file conversions worked without problems. (I use two separate files for different purposes.)

I find the UI changes mostly unimportant ... and I'm talking about 3 years worth of changes, folks! I haven't found any significant functional improvements either. They haven't even bothered improving the login process for financial institutions (like my bank) which are using what I'll call multi-step login (user id, password, and personal question selected from a list).

One annoying change is the "Community" logo on the top right -- yeah, I really wanted that one, it'll improve my life dramatically. This could easily have been an icon on the toolbar, so that those who want it keep it, those who don't can remove it.

Ok, so far it's all break-even, assuming that you accept the idea of buying the software more like a subscription than a one-time purchase. The big negative so far is that the app is much slower now: apparently there's a lot more on-the-fly calculation going on now when you switch screens or change data.

Recommendation: If you use Quicken, and want to continue doing so, don't be afraid of this upgrade. Don't rush to it, either.

As everyone knows, Intuit is not really putting in a lot of effort into adding new capabilities into Quicken, because it's now a small part of their overall business. So no surprise, there are very few differences between 2012 & 2011, despite all the marketing claims. In fact, I'd have a hard time telling you what significant improvements I've seen in the last 10 years or so.

The one material change I do see in this version is an improvement: My bank uses a two-factor authentication method, meaning that it requires a second "secret fact" in addition to the password. Previously, when updating the four accounts I have at this bank, Quicken would ask me to enter this second key four times, meaning they were logging in separately each time. Now I only have to enter it once, implying that only one login is used to download all four accounts. Might seem minor, but removing tedium is always good.

Other than that? You get the new tax rates. And some user interface improvements in a few areas, which I can't comment on because I don't use them. (Budgeting for example: I've always found Quicken budgeting pretty useless, requires a lot of setup and offers very little value for the work.) No improvements in reporting, I've seen none there in many years. No improvements in the portfolio management area, or in the tax reporting area, both of these remain grossly inadequate.

I've been using Quicken for more than 20 years now, and will continue to use it until something better comes along. It's useful, and adequate, for recordkeeping, an electronic ledger if you will. But that's all it is, it's not going to do more for you. I find myself relying on (and paying for) other tools for managing my financial life.

Initial Review 6 Dec 2015

This is my first report, which I will update down the road after I've made more progress.

Initial download from Amazon and installation was completely trouble-free (Windows 7 64-bit). No problems with warnings, glitches, updates, or anything else. The only oddity (minor) was that after the initial updates it failed to automatically start the program, after saying it would. When I did start it up, it quickly found the various copies of my 2014 tax files (I save versions as I go, in case I make a serious error and need to roll back). Imports from the file I selected were clean and trouble-free. My tax situation this year includes self-employment income, investment income, foreign income (not just mutual funds), itemized deductions, college expenses, 529 fund payouts, and Roth conversions.

The interview hasn't changed much that I noticed. I switched back and forth between the interview and the forms view, as I often do, to understand what was going on under the covers. It didn't take too long for me to enter all my current numbers (many of them estimates, of course) and get a sense of my full tax picture. For state taxes, TT had already started on my state return (based on my home state), but asked me to confirm that it was the free state I wanted to use (extra states have additional cost, e.g., if you live and work in different states). The state tax return was also trouble-free and looked correct.

Two glitches to report so far, hopefully these will be corrected. Both are related to college costs, and both can cost you real money.
(1) My son's college charges a required fee that it doesn't include in the 1098T. It's a qualified expense for the 529 fund, and there's a place for it on the form, but TT doesn't ask for it or allow it during the interview. You sort of have to know the mechanics and go into the right form to add this item. Not user-friendly, and can lead to higher taxes than you owe. Bad.
(2) The "optimization" of the various education credits is terrible, and can lead to bad results if you let the program do what it chooses. In my case TT reserved a huge part of the 529 funds withdrawn for the AOC (don't worry if you don't know what that is), which led to some of it becoming taxable. There was no optimization -- I was able to do much better with simple trial-and-error. Bad.

One other thing I noticed: there doesn't appear to be a simple way to find and correct the health insurance figure (in the business income section). It's hard to find in the interview, and I couldn't find a way to change it in the forms (ran into a circular reference between two forms each saying go change the other one). This part of the program hasn't changed from last year. Not a big problem, just something to be aware of.

Overall, I'm satisfied. Still a reasonable program for the money, still does a decent job at reducing my tax computation and filing hassles.

Update 22 Feb 2016:

Overall I'm still reasonably happy with TT. Some specific comments:

(1) The college fees issue I mentioned above is still in the software, which I think means that it will "never" be corrected. It's important to enter this data correctly, obviously. Further, it might affect your state tax as well: in MA, it matters in the computation of the college tuition deduction.

(2) The optimization of the American Opportunity Credit is now corrected, it works the way it should.

(3) I had a problem with the MA tuition deduction calculation works -- in my first run in December this wasn't done correctly by TT, so it over-indicated (by more than $2000) how much I would gain from this. So now I find that I'm paying the state instead of getting a refund. Would have been nice to know that before I had to pay my Jan estimated tax installment.

(4) The handling of Form 1116 (for foreign tax credit) is very poorly implemented. TT prompts you during error checking to fill in some required "explain this line" forms, instead of doing so during the interview. Also, the explanations are usually so simple that TT has the information needed to pre-fill these in, instead of asking the user to hunt down where the numbers came from. Also, if you're not careful, Form 1116 might calculate your foreign tax credits incorrectly, by excluding certain foreign income. I've found that one MUST review this form manually and make corrections directly in the form and in the relevant 1099 forms, in order to make sure everything is done correctly. (I've been doing this for years now, there's been no improvement here.)

Let's get the obvious negatives stated first. Like many other long-term quicken users, I'd use something else if there was a reasonable option. (I've tried pretty much everything else.) This program is old, clunky, buggy, etc. etc. It hasn't been improved significantly in more than 10 years, really. Areas that need complete revamping, such as reports, haven't been touched. Using it in a modern "access from anywhere" way (i.e., data on the cloud, mobile access) is stupidly limited and about as ugly as a 1980s software engineer might have designed. BUT ... it remains useful if you like to manage your finances in detail, and use your records for filing taxes and making financial plans.

So this 2017 product doesn't look and feel much different from the 2015 version it replaced in my household. Yes, some colors and icons changed, but only the Quicken people consider those significant. (In well-designed modern products those are user-customizable.) That's both good and bad: at least there are no nasty surprises.

Conversion of files (why on earth do they keep doing this?) was error-prone: I had to do it several times to finally get a conversion that didn't lose months of transactions. Don't ask, it's all mysterious nonsense. (And no, validate/super-validate didn't fix things.)

But once I was finally there, all my files (I have several) did convert correctly, the reports work, downloads work (I had to re-enter my Intuit pwd -- Quicken id conversion hasn't happened yet). Nothing exciting to report, but also not quite as dreadful as some reviews will have you expect.

So, if you're a long-term Quicken user who finds it necessary to continue using the program, this is a reasonable update that's good for another 3 years. (If they do go to a subscription model next year as rumors have it, I hope that Q17 users will be able to avoid that annual charge until 2020.)

If you're not a long-term user, perhaps you want to consider alternatives, such as Mint.
