I am no expert but I can product high-quality results in a shorter time span with Pinnacle, just because the application’s layout is more straightforward and easy to follow.

Though much older versions of Pinnacle Studio were a little easier on my system than this version, Version 23 is a good improvement over last year’s Version 22 which made my system work a lot harder. Some serious under-the-hood improvements have gone into this version which for me would be enough to move to this version. If you are looking for a video production solution and want one that is easy to understand and produces good results, this is a good choice.

I have been using TurboTax since 2007 and so far it has worked out well for me. I like the interface, I like the way it imports last-year’s data and I like how it allows me to prepare and e-file returns for everyone in my household with one license. A new tax season is on us, and as such so is a new TurboTax.

This is equally bad if not worse than not requiring activation, and in the long run this will cost them business. So far, my copy only needed to be activated one time, and hopefully that’s where it will stay. If it does do that to me, I will update this review and will switch software moving forward.

There are two ways to install, from a CD and from a download. I used the CD as I have always done and it was smooth and relatively painless. It took maybe 5 minutes to install, and I suspect the download version will install faster. Regardless, I am up and running.

The interface is familiar, a Q&A style of back-and-forth between the software and the user. Even someone who is afraid of the computer should have no problem understanding and using this software. It is designed to be user-friendly, straightforward, easy and concise in getting the information it needs.

As always, it imported last year’s return without a hitch.

I haven’t finished my return yet as I have not yet received all of tax documents from some of my expected sources, but once I do I’ll e-file everything. Assuming that process is unchanged, it’s quick and easy using TurboTax’s built-in functions for e-filing both federal and state.

So far, my experience has been positive but I am still relatively early in the process. I expect no issues, unless the registration problem becomes a real headache. If Intuit has ironed out this problem, then TurboTax is a very good solution for filing your taxes this year. I will revisit this review and update as I find changes and/or issues, but for now I have had a positive experience so far.

I have been using PhotoDirector since version 8, and while it has some limitations (it is nowhere near as powerful as some of the other photo editors out there) it has a place in my arsenal of tools. For quick adjustments and some moderate photo editing it is a good tool for the asking price.

I will start by saying that there are photo editors available that cost less and do more advanced editing. When I want to make very detailed edits, such as removing objects or working in layers to adjust colors on very specific things in the photo, PhotoDirector is not the tool I generally use for these tasks. It can do these things, and it can do more, but every tool is different and some are easier to use than others. It is not a suitable replacement for a tool like PhotoShop, regardless, which has far more functionality going well beyond the basics.

For me, the greatest strength that PhotoDirector brings to the table is template-based quick adjustments. It comes with a set of presets already, and these are great for applying global changes to a photo quickly. There are some for working specifically with portraits, color and lighting enhancements, and even B/W filters with varying levels of exposure and contrast settings. The adjustments made can be taken as-is or the user can make additional tweaks to a variety of factors - temperature, exposure compensation, saturation, contrast and more.

The program provides access to a community where there are hundreds of additional, user-content templates as well. This requires creating an account there, for which there is no cost, and after setting up an account you can download as many of the presets as you desire. If you have a very wide variety of photographs you wish to process, the community-provided presets offer a lot of flexibility and are a big time saver. As with the presets included with the application, these can be used as-is or as a starting point.

Loading a lot of presets in the application can bog things down a lot. I probably have 30 presets downloaded, and with the older version I was using it could take close to a minute to load up an image because it ran through all of the presets and cached the rendered image - or the application would just hang. In this version the process of loading all of the presets seems to have been improved and the application loads images a lot faster. And, so far I have had no crashes or hangs.

In addition to providing photo editing, this application is a capable photo organizer and can help you get your image catalog straight. It is similar to a lot of other image organizers out there in format and layout (and even the color scheme), so if you have used other applications for organizing your photos this will be familiar ground.

This is neither the most capable nor the cheapest photo editing and organization tool available, but what it does it does well. It's well-suited for those looking for a tool for quick adjustments as well as keeping their photos organized. If you are looking for absolute control over your images and want to make highly complex and intricate adjustments this is probably not the tool you want, but if you want to make some easy to intermediate adjustments or want a template-based approach as a starting point, this is a fine tool for the job.

The package isn't very intuitive... so you'll definitely need the tutorals. But as far as being a very good tool for manga artists: it lives up to its billing. There are some things it misses (such as the ability to do graduating backgrounds). The most annoying thing I've found is that while it can export files in Photoshop format... it loses all layering when doing so. This is fairly annoying.

Most folks who use this package admit that the rough work and general layout / artistry is done in this package, then switching to a more powerful graphics package (such as Photoshop) to do the finish work. I don't know that all artists will find that necessary, as this package is powerful enough of itself to go from beginning to end work. All in all, I don't think this can be beat for the price. It does what it says it will do. Has a rather steep learning curve... but once it's learned, performance is fairly good. Like I stated, there are some annoyances, but all in all worth the price. Those who buy this may also want to buy POSER DEBUT, which is excellent for use as an "artists doll" to get exactly the right positioning and poses from which to draw. Both packages together: $100 (or less on Amazon). Can't beat that with a stick.

This is a very basic game that is fun to play. The concept: join as many individual blocks together as possible, to make units of four or more "vanishing" shapes. You get points for larger shapes, but as everything four or above triggers the score, one has to think ahead to make larger blocks.

PROS:
* Semi-habit-forming but not too bad. I get "tired" of playing it within a few minutes, which helps avoid it becoming addictive. Yet it's fun enough to keep on my tablet... so that's a good thing. Doesn't take up too much of my time that way, but it's there if I want it.
* Easy to play. Children should love it.
* Colorful. Babies and infants may enjoy the bright colors, movable shapes and sound.

CONS:
* It's somewhat tricky to figure out how you're scoring. Since the heavy majority of scoring is automatic (domino effect) it's very difficult to actually gauge one's skill level while playing. I found myself often thinking I'd played a "great game"... only to have a dismal score, while at other times I thought I'd played lousy and would score amazingly high. Actual skill therefore seems relatively unrelated to end-score.
* There's only so "good" you can get at this. There's a ceiling, it's easy to reach that ceiling, and no where to go from there.

Bottom line it's a fun game, better than some, and is indeed mildly compulsive.

Once you figure out that this requires two copies (one for the phone, the other for the computer), this is a dandy little program. It allows you to create new file folders on the receiving end, transfers files both directions, and works across your internal wifi network so there's no need to connect USB cords. After the initial setup and pairing, it's quite easy to use.

The thing to realize is the system doesn't work at all until BOTH programs are involved and operational. When you turn one on, it gives you an access screen and then just sits there. When you turn the second program on, they automatically 'find' each other and the transfer box pops up. You can upload or download, create file folders, and do just about anything you need to do in the case of file transfer.

This program was somewhat essential for use with the Amazon Fire Table series, since the HD10 does not have the ability to transfer files by USB (which is one of the things I dislike about the Fire Tablet). But this program fixes all that. You install it on your Fire tablet, install it on your computer, turn both programs on, and they transfer just about anything to anywhere.

I got this app when it was the FAOTD and never played it until last week. I have played it almost every day since then. It has several variations of the game that keep game playing interesting. It allows you to 'pencil in' possible answers, which I use every game. Has multiple difficulty levels, not just easy and hard. I like playing on moderate right now, but I am working my way to more advanced levels. The best thing about this app has to be the hint button. If you get stuck and don't know how to make your next move, it gives you a hint and highlights what area it is referring to. If you can't figure out what that hint is trying to tell you, you can push the '+' button to get that hint simplified. Still don't understand? Hit the '+' button one more time and they tell you flat out what it means. I've used the hints twice and they have drastically improved my technique. I now understand the game so much more!
Bottom line: Would I recommend this app to a friend? Yes.
Would I spend $2 on this app? Yes.

I ordered the free version at first for the kids I babysit. They had a lot of fun coloring their pages, but then we found out they could only save up to 3 of the pics with the free version, So being the pushover I am, I went ahead and ordered the paid version. It was worth the .99 cents to make the kiddos happy and I even colored a page to look like my own parrot :)

The birdie pics are cute and range from really simple drawings to those with more detail. Quite a bit of colors to choose from - no blending of your own colors though, There's 3 different brush sizes + 3 erasers that correspond with the different brush sizes. If you make a mistake, you can either erase it or simply color over it with the paint brush,

The only real "complaint" I can think of, is that when one tries to color in the background, if you get to close to the colors along the side of the screen, it's very easy to change the color. The kids wished there was a "color fill" option to color the background - that would have saved time and frustration since the brushes are rather small.

If you like birdies and want a very simple, fun way to pass the time with the kids, this app is a good choice ;)

I purchased this as the FAPOTD a few months ago and have really enjoyed playing it. Basically you are creating a "word tree" starting from the ground up and branching out with different associated words. While some words might fit in multiple spots, there is usually only one correct spot which makes the game more challenging.

Surprisingly, there are minimal permissions--rare for a FAPOTD. The only reason I gave the game 4 stars is because you can't simply restart a level if you've become hopelessly screwed up in your word choices. If you start the level over, it gives you a whole new set of words. Now of course that adds to the game's versatility, but I do wish it gave the option of starting the level over with the same puzzle.

Very fun game. If you enjoy word association games, I think you'll enjoy Next Word.

I just downloaded Trigonometrics as the FAOTD. I think at this point, the name is more interesting than the app itself.

When the app opens, it automatically starts filling the screen with a spirograph. You can attempt to be interactive with it by touching the screen, but it's kinda pointless on a small phone as the screen fills so fast. Since the spirographs are
auto-generated, the mystery buttons at the bottom of the screen only add to the "chaos." While it's possible to clear the screen with the last button on the right, this only lasts a few seconds before the app generates a new spirograph.

I will have to trust other reviews in terms of adware/analytics as I have no way to test that aspect of the app. It appears that the developer has not included anything that would invade your privacy.While that's a refreshing change for the FAOTD, the developer also did not include any instructions as to the point of those cute little buttons. I have many drawing apps that I have to figure out what the buttons do on my own. The difference, however, is that I am the one generating the design at my own pace. I can see the changes made by pressing each button. This app fills the screen so fast with the spirographs, pressing the buttons only adds to the mess.

Trigonometrics would be so much more fun if you could actually create the spirograph without the app doing it automatically. The lack of explanation of the buttons would be forgivable if you had time to see what the different nuances are with each button press. I'm hoping the developer will improve upon this app, but until then, I will play with the spirograph app I got for the kids. At least then I can draw my own designs.

First: My opinions and bias comes from a "Samsung Galaxy S4" and a "Win XP" desktop. I have used handheld computers since the days of the Hewlett Packard HP95LX.

If you can use Windows Explorer or any other hierarchical file manager, B-Folders works the same way. You create folders within folders until you find where to create a document. No limits.

B-Folders has both a mobile version and a PC version, but you only pay $29 for the PC version; the device copies are really FREE! The data stays on your devices. That means you don't have to pay "rent" for a cloud, and you don't need an internet connection to access your info, which saves money! (No thanks, "Evernote".)

I think that synchronization with B-Folders is elegant! A sync session between any 2 devices can be initiated by either one of them. There is no limit to the number of devices that can be synced, but you can only sync 2 at a time. We have 2 phones and a PC, so that is perfect for our needs. My wife and I had some quality time together while I showed her how syncing worked. We sat in front of the PC with our phones in hand. She laughed out loud as we synched notes back and forth from phone to phone with the PC in the middle. She would create a note on her phone then sync with the PC. In just a few seconds her message appeared on the PC. Then I did the same. It was fun and we had a good time doing it.

B-Folders comes with a small collection of forms such as Password, Banking, and Credit Card, but you are free to add or remove fields from those. You can create your own templates too. (I wish it would allow me to change fonts, or bold or underline text.)

"Security" is very strong! It applies encryption and passwords on all platforms. Many other apps I have tried, including my old favorite, "ListPro", store data in text format which means the data is unprotected even if the file requires a password. B-Folders will close up everything after a set amount of time which you specify. That's great! If you loose your device your data will be locked within a short time.

As for "customer service", I can't speak to that yet, because I haven't had a problem yet! That's best kind of customer service!

To wrap it up: For 3 months I have spent day-and-night looking for flexible, secure, and easy-to-use data store that does not use the cloud. B-Folders is where I am ending my search. As always, your mileage may vary.

For someone who has never liked to play crossword puzzles I thoroughly enjoy this game. You are given several categories of games to choose from; for example, people, places, things, etc. Then you select one of many games in your chosen category.

At the top of the game is a list of seven phrases - each phrase suggests something about the word that belongs to it (similar to the way a crossword puzzle would). To the right of the phrase you are given the number of letters required to spell the word you must guess.

Below the 7 phrases is a bunch of word fragments. Each fragment has 1 or more letters. You construct the words that correspond to the phrases by tapping on a fragment. When you are ready to commit to your word and phrase you tap on the CHECK button. If your word is the correct answer to one of the phrases in the list, the game places a check mark next to the phrase. Of course, if your word doesn't match anything - nothing happens.

The game kindly allows you to reshuffle the word fragments as many times as you like. This can help you see words from a different perspective, and I use it often.

I'm sure that everyone has their special way to arrive at answers to the phrases. I seem to do better when I just consider one phrase at a time. Let's say the phrase is MAKES THINGS FALL. I would naturally think of the word GRAVITY. I compare the given number of letters allowed for that phrase to the number of letters in the word gravity. If the count matches, then I look in the fragments for the pieces that would spell gravity. If I find them, great. If that doesn't work I move on to the next phrase. I don't linger on one item for long. Then I loop back to the top and start over again. Eventually, there is only one word left and the answer is obvious. So, really, you only have to think about 6 of the phrases.

The game offers a few hints for free. Of course you can buy more either with money or the points they give you each day that you play the game. So far I haven't used any hints.

I like many types of games. The one I choose to play depends on my circumstances at the moment, but this game is one of my favorites for when I just want to relax and play something that won't keep me from sleeping, or if I'm in a doctor's office.

Deadeye Decker

The concept is easy enough - just turn all the squares to the dark side. But doing it is a bit like trying to kill an ameba by stomping on it. Whenever you tap on a square to flip its color it also causes every adjoining square to flip color too; that is, it toggles the squares that are left, right, up and down from the square you touch. It does not affect the diagonal squares. You can touch either color. I think I may have found a method that will result in a win every time.

The scheme is to plan a set of 4 or 8 taps in a symmetrical pattern without considering what is happening until you complete the pattern you have planned. Discipline. Don't stop to look until you complete your pattern. I really don't think it matters much which pattern you choose. Just make a different plan for each round until you win.

First play the game to understand how, at first, it seems like there is no way to win. Then re-read what I try to explain here. It will make more sense that way.

The secret seems to be to PLAN A SYMMETRICAL PATTERN OF TAPS IN ADVANCE with no regard for what happens.

For example, plan on tapping all 4 OUTTER corners; just do it and don't look at the changes until you have tapped all 4 corners. Just for fun, tap on all 4 corners again; the board returns to its original pattern. Neat. Now tap on the outside corners again.

From now on, look at the board and notice any symmetrical pattern that resulted from your last round of taps. If you see a pattern developing - you can use it to plan your next pattern of 4-8 taps.

Let's say your next plan is to tap all 4 INNER squares. Again execute your plan of tapping those 4 squares without being at all concerned for what happens.

Your pattern plan MUST BE SYMMETRICAL. Just choose a different pattern each round.

Continue doing this until you win. It will kind of surprise you when it happens - at least it surprises me, because I don't actually see it happen.

I hope this works for everyone. :-)

My wife and I play this game a lot, but every once in a while we get stuck. We were using Google to look up the answers, but then she discovered a quicker way.

If you get stuck on a puzzle use this trick.

1. Write down, on a piece of paper or whatever you like, every character in the list you are given. Spread the letters out. This will make the answer easier to identify.

2. Now exit back to the main menu of the game.

3. Click the PLAY button to go back to the same puzzle you are having trouble with.

4. Notice that you have been given a different set of characters for the same puzzle.

5. Compare each of the new letters to the letters you wrote on the paper - one by one.

6. Underline every character that was there before. (ignore the new characters)

7. Repeat the process from step-2 above.

8. Repeat from step-2 2 or 3 times, or until you realise that there is a sub set of characters that have 2 or 3 underlines. Those are the letters you need to spell the answer to your puzzle.

Of course, you can also go to Google and look it up there, but I think that takes longer.

Now that's better than paying for hints!

It's a good product to have, but on the Kindle and phones it became a bit frustrating. The constant need to update itself, and the stress-inducing messages that the devices may potentially be at risk ended up encouraging us to uninstall from the mobile devices in favor of something else. We don't keep data switched on our mobile devices all the time because we prefer apps that can function offline rather than installing data-hog apps that chew through data like they're obsessed with it. While this product's downloads are small in byte-size compared to others, and seem to install flawlessly, I don't want to be a slave to the apps on our devices. I don't want to have to be constantly reviewing and responding to messages. When data was turned off, which is most of the time on our phones, which we use mostly for calls, calendars, and the occasional text message, we kept getting notices that we needed to update and that our devices were at risk. Maybe the developers could add a toggle or setting that would stop notifications when data is off and simply allow it to quietly update itself when the data is switched back on again.

That being said, Malwarebytes has a trusted and true rep and puts out good quality products. For those whose data is unlimited and that is turned on all the time, I definitely recommend it. It can quietly update itself in the background with limited need for interaction and attention from the end user.

Not having a lot of experience with streaming apps I, naively, assumed HBO Now would be like Netflix. I could sign up for an account and then log in with whatever device I had. Not true.

If you setup HBO Now through your Fire TV it gets married to your Amazon devices. You can't sign into a Roku or TiVo that might have HBO Now in a different room like you can with Netflix. You have to purchase or move an Amazon Fire device in any place you want to use your HBO Now subscription.

The app lets you choose between two different fireworks presentations. The first one is the larger "aerial bomb" type fireworks with lots of green and reds. However this entire first clip is only about 15 seconds long, then it repeats. You don't notice the repeat immediately, it is gracefully edited, but it gets boring eventually like any 15 second clip would.

The 2nd option is more rapid fire, smaller, explosions, more white, lots of smaller fireworks leaving trails across the screen. A lot of smoke can be seen in the background. This clip is longer than the first, but still less than a minute. I estimate maybe 45 seconds or so.

I gave this 4 stars because 3.5, which is what I really want to give it, rounds up to 4, and honestly, I have come to expect such apps repeat short video clips over and over.

I remember decades ago on a Windows 95 computer Fireworks "screensavers" that were randomly generated fireworks, sure they didn't look as spectacular as HD footage, but they were so much more fun because it was unique. You could pick the colors, pick the number of simultaneous fireworks. THAT is what I really want someone to make. Give me an app that generates a random/unique fireworks display, not some 15 second professionally recorded clip.

Would love the ability to check/uncheck a big list of cameras and setup my own "channel" that changes between selected cameras only at a time interval I specify. Perhaps even an option to add custom stream URLs.

I think once it has all or even some of these improvements it will be a solid 4 or 5 star app. It's nice to see what's going on in the world.

If you have a party going on and you're looking for something to do besides board and/or card games Fibbage works well. Almost everyone has their own controller already if they have a smartphone of any type one them, a laptop or computer of any kind in the room can also be used to play the game. It would be 5 stars but for the money I hoped for a far larger database to pull "questions" from. It's probably no worse than any home board game, eventually you've seen all the cards, but a physical limitation need not be accepted in a digital world.

Under Time Warner Cable the app worked decently on Amazon Fire TVs. Not that it became Spectrum we're told our TWC app needs to be upgraded and they will not work until you give the OK to upgrade, but once you upgrade you're told the app is not compatible with your device. So the Spectrum "upgrade" means many Fire TV customers lost the ability to watch cable. At least some Fire TV customers bought the Fire TV because the TWC app was working on it. Very annoying. Spectrum should at least maintain what TWC had provided.

This app was created by a great supporter of the Amazon Fire TV and fellow customer looking to make life easier for other Fire TV customers. It originally was used solely for downloading files to your device but since morphed into a basic web browser with download abilities that even the official Silk browser doesn't (yet?) have.

This is an indispensable utility for "power users" who know what they are doing or those just following instructions of a random guide or youtube video.

If you find this app doesn't work as expected it is far more likely the problem is with the website you are trying to access than the app itself.

You have no option to change trains or locations and worse, despite the description, this does not show "Live" streams. You can see for yourself when it's middle of the night somewhere and it's sunny when they are showing the location. The fact it displays a clock on the video with the time in various time zones makes me feel like they were intentionally deceptive. Why would I need a clock if the footage isn't live? Youtube doesn't show me a clock when I am watching recorded videos there.

That said it's hard to complain when it's totally free. Some people might still find it interesting, I unfortunately am not one of them. Should they find a way to show actual live video one day I'd be in, I'd probably even pay a small fee for it- if it was truly live and I could choose the train or location.

I already wrote a large and detailed review as to why this product is a poor value and suggesting lots of better options, but it is no longer here, sorry to all interested, but I don't feel like trying to recall and rewrite at this time.

Edit

OK, ready to try to rewrite my review. First off, when I purchased it was required to leave a review to unlock one of the games, I did not like this in a paid app one bit. This seems to have been removed. Next is the games. 3 of the 9 are available for free in the demo version. Another one is available for free in the Barnyard Games demo version, only there it is listed as ages 2+ and here as 4+, odd. This leaves 5 unique games for 2 dollars.

One of these games is a puzzle game that is the worst puzzle game we own, there are many free options that are much better such as the Kids Puzzles series as well as Kid's Love Puzzles. These apps control much better and have a lot more variety and actual difficulty levels. My 2yo can do 24 piece jigsaw puzzles independently, so a little 4 piece puzzle is boring for him. Pieces that snap back to the original position whenever pressure is not well maintained make the game very frustrating.

Another game is the memory game. There are tons of these available for free. Try Kid's Match'em, Giraffe's Matching, or Animal Memory for nicer looking free options.

This leaves 3 games for my 2 dollars. Addition, Subtraction, and Spelling. My son is too young for the spelling and subtraction, so I can't comment on the them too much. They seem to be made well enough. The addition game is fine. I would add an equals sign, but it works as inteded and is easy enough for my son to use.

I just don't think that the 3 remaining games are a good value at 3 dollars and that is all I really got for my purchase.

My final complaint is the praise. I have my degree in the field of psychology and have worked with children for years and I am against constant praise due to the negative effects it can have. Just wish I could either turn it off or that it was more intermittent and less over the top.

That about sums up what I remember from my original review. I hope this one doesn't dissapear too!

I grabbed this game for the 99 cent promo price and am glad that I did. My son is only 2 and barely able to play just 2 of the games, but there is a lot of good content here that will grow with him.

There are 10 games total, half relating to mathmatics and half to language. There are no bad games, but some are more interesting then others. I like the pattern and ordering games the best. My son is able to do the ordering game on the lowest level and the spelling game on the 3 letter setting and likes the word bingo, but needs a little verbal coaching to pick out the correct word.

In Patterns there is a sequence of shapes and/or pictures and the child is asked to pick which one comes next. This sort of thing is usually very fun for kids around this age.

In ordering the goal is to touch the balloons in the correct order, such as alphabetical, biggest to smallest, etc. My son really enjoys this on level 1.

Advanced counting works just like the Kintergarten and Preschool apps counting, but rather than counting by ones, it asks the child to count by 2's, 3's, 5's and 10's. I wish this game had a difficulty selector that would determine total number of balls on the screen at once to help with learning the concept on smaller numbers. I would prefer if larger numbers over 100 did not include the word and, they no longer say one hundred and one, they now just say one hundred one.

Fractions is a nice visual game where the child is asked to find the picture that represents the stated fraction, such as a pie with 2 of four pieces shaded for 2/4ths. I would like to see a choice on this one to have the answers remain stationary for children with visual tracking difficulties.

The addtion and Subtraction is much like that in the Kindergarten and Preschool app, but goes to much higher numbers, my son is also getting the hang of addition only for the smaller numbers.

Word bingo is a fun concept, kid's this age always love bingo. The main problem I had here was related to volume, some words were hard to hear even at max volume (in fact the whole game is pretty quiet at max volume). I'm not sure I like the way that the word switches if you get one wrong, I think it would be best to let the child guess again until they get the right answer. I would also like to see the word written on the tile with the picture after the tile is flipped to strenthen the association.

Compound words seems like the sort of game I would have enjoyed as a child. The goal is just to match two parts of compound words together, such as cat and nip to make catnip. I got one wrong myself, apparently backlight wasn't the compound word the game was looking for.

Contractions is simply choosing the contraction such as can't and matching it with the full meaning can not. Pretty straightforward.

Verbs, Nouns, and Adjectives is just like Fractions in that the answers float around and you have to pick out the right answer. I would like to see a choice to have the answers remain stationary on this one as well.

Overall there are a lot of good games included in this collection that cover quite a few areas of first grade education. I would like to see more apps covering subjects other than just reading and math, but this game at least covers a variety of reading and math related activities. It would also be nice if rather than gush constant praise the game would go with a simple correct or yes every once in a while. I am happy with my purchase and would recommend this game to children in the target range.

I've been using this app for about five months now and I've been VERY satisfied so far. This is an incredible app to use when you want to learn new languages, although I have to say that you have to have at least the most basic knowledge of your target language, e.g. it's alphabet, basic pronunciation, etc. But once you have that, there's nothing better than Duolingo.

I'm using Kindle Fire HD and can't do the speaking exercises (Kindle's microphone doesn't work on this app), but you can have the option of turning that off and just use the type option instead. You still have the part of the lessons where you'll have to listen to a recording and type what you hear. The recording uses the normal speed for speech, and if that's too fast for you, there's an available option for a slow version (or "turtle" version - cute term ;)).

The best part in learning through Duolingo is the Discussion Page, where learners can access from every exercise page. There, learners may discuss any problem, ask other advanced learners/native speakers about any question you want to ask concerning the lesson, etc. 99.9% of the participants are friendly and very helpful. To me this portion of Duolingo is what makes it unique and the most fun.

I've read from other reviews that Duolingo requires you to have a Facebook account in order to register. This is simply not accurate. It does let you use your Facebook account to register, if you had one anf IF YOU WANTED TO, but you can always choose not to, and YOU DEFINITELY CAN REGISTER WITHOUT USING A FACEBOOK ACCOUNT!

So, yes, you should definitely try this app. It's really, really worth it, I promise! :)

First, let me start that I adore the original Castaway. This third one, Lost World, is disappointing, because of the major changes:

1. The stuff you used to be able to do spending "pearls" now cost "emeralds", which are WAY TOO DIFFICULT TO ACQUIRE or WAY TOO EXPENSIVE (they could be bought with real money - lot of it!) Pearls are almost worthless now. You need an extra space for your back pack? EMERALDS. Need to buy simple stuff from the store? EMERALDS.

2. When you need to make the special dishes for the tribe or whoever, they're now TIMED. You need to make tools, TIMED. You would feel like you're playing Facebook games. For these TIMED tasks, you could have HOURS, even DAYS, of waiting to do. While making the tools you need, boars are attacking you and you CANNOT DO ANYTHING, because even if you already have the bow, you couldn't shoot these pesky animals (game hasn't allowed you yet, until [I guess] you've defeated the FIRST BIG-BOSS enemy).

There are more major changes that I find really disappointing. The "pearls" now are almost worthless. EVERYTHING CRUCIAL TO KEEP PLAYING THE GAME MUST BE BOUGHT USING ONLY THE FRIGGIN' EMERALDS! I wish there are ways for G5 to change them back to the the original Castaway style that they could issue updates for.

Because of these changes, I'm shaving off 3 stars in my review. BTW, this is NOT a sequel, despite what so many reviewers call it. It's a parallel story of the (almost) same castaways from the original Castaway, with one change in the original characters, plus a couple new ones.

I'm giving this two stars for a nice storyline, and for the beautiful graphics. The game also lags big time, by the way.

This game recently was "updated" and added an option to play using Spanish. While this change is welcome and can actually help those who want to check on their Spanish vocab for whatever reason, this game gives the letters "w" and "k" which are hardly ever seen in Spanish! It also lacks the "ñ" which is a 'very' Spanish letter. How weird is that? They had just an update, again, and it says that "w" and "k" are not going to be activated anymore. Well, this is just not true - those two culprit letters are still very much present. And the "w" is one of the letters with the stone/gem which you'd want to use if you want to get all the letters with the jewel to completely complete the game.

Remove the almost useless letters and add in the really-needed ones (ñ, ü - and how about more "U's" every time you activate the "q"? The "q" is practically useless in Spanish if the "u" isn't present, you know?!) and maybe you'll get 5 stars from me. For the meantime you get one.

EDIT:
I'm editing this because after the 3rd update for the Spanish, the unusable letters, "k" and "w" are gone. I also found out that the regular "n" and "u" can be used in place of the Spanish "ñ" and "ü". What's even greater is that the game started crashing (nope, that's not what's great), but after contacting the developer the game is now absolutely going smooth. This is what's great. That the developer has been really into it, doing everything and finding the issue that was causing the crash. Sometimes games/apps do get issues - that just reality. They're made by humans, afterall. But when the developer actually cares and does something about an issue, well, what else can anyone complain about? What I'm saying is that I couldn't be happier by how the Word Wow Big City's developer for into the issue and fixed it! And now I'm changing my review from 1 star to 5! Wish I could give this game a 10!

So yeah, 5 stars!

First of all, I love every single Radiangames game that I have ever played, which is quite a few. This one, their most recent (as of right now when this review was submitted,) has no exception. I loved the first game, and I love this one as well!
When I first got the game, I found literally an absolute TON of differences from the first game, [[ASIN:B00JRH6KMO Inferno+]]. There's a LOT more stuff and stuff like that. Also, at first, I didn't like that instead of bombs, which would defeat the black enemies in the first game, there were missiles, which defeat the new red enemies in the second game. I didn't like the missiles at first because they weren't unlimited; you had to purchase them in the game store using the gold currency you collect in-game during missions. But, I then found out that it is a LOT easier to get gold in the second game. I don't know if anyone else experienced this, but I found myself having a lot of gold literally before I knew it. It was so awesome, I no longer had a problem with the missiles. I understood why they had limited ammo. The missiles are a little overpowered and should only be used if necessary. If they were unlimited, even the bosses that come, like, every ten levels, would probably be easy to defeat. I do like the missiles though because (remember those extra stuff and stuff like that I mentioned earlier?) They are specifically made to destroy things like special barriers, secret walls, and of course, those annoying red enemies (they are more harder than those slow black enemies from the first game!).
With that out of the way, I do have one complaint that surprisingly didn't affect my rating, but I feel should be recognized for Radiangames. Why in the world did you take out the razor sheild?!?!?! The razor sheild in the first game was amazingly awesome and I found myself using it ALL the time, but, it's not in the second game. Maybe the fact that it was used, maybe even over used, was the fact that they took it out in the sequel. In its place, it is replaced with, I don't even remember what they were called. Abilities? Maybe. IDK. I won't talk about them so you can just figure them out for yourself. Same goes for the weapons upgrades. I'll just tell you this: upgrading is not the same for the first game, which I didn't like at first, but then got the hang of and eventually liked it purely because the rest of the have is AWESOME.
I'm sorry for the fact that I'm rambling on and on, but I just want to talk about one last thing. One word: mösic! The music in every single Radiangames… uh… game, is the best electro music that I have every hered in my life, (other then Eclipse by Minecraft Universe,) and it's another reason why I love to play their games. If their music was on Spotify, they would make a lot of money off of me because I'd listen to their music all day long on Spotify. That's for much I love their music. It really gets me pumped up for the next level. I'm surprised Radiangames hasn't made one of those games where your weapons are synced with the music and soot to the best and stuff.
Anyway, thanks for reading my review on Inferno 2. If you haven't played the first game, [[ASIN:B00JRH6KMO Inferno+]], then I recommend you to play it first, then play this second game. If you're wondering, "is it worth the buy?" I would say, "yes! It's awesome and you should buy it now before the world ends!" I hope that I have helped you choose weather or not to buy this awesome game. Thanks!

I have played a number of escape games, and this one is probably just like all the others. Let me first day that tree only reason that I got it was because it is the free app of the day for the same day that I am writing this review.
Okay, so the first thing that I'll talk about the have is the story. First of all, lots of escape games don't have a story. You just start out in a room, and since it's an escape game, you just know what to do. Find a way to get through the door and go on to the next level. This game has a bit of a story. Apparently, your character is in Hollywood and wants to play as the villain in a movie they're making, but the director says that in order to get the part, you have to solve some puzzles that the Hollywood people has set up. So, naturally, the puzzles are to escape various Hollywood settings such as movie sets and stuff.
One of the things that I don't like about the game is how you actually escape the levels, and what I mean by that is that you aren't' actually just escaping through a door set right out in front of you. Sometimes it's a window or something, so you don't actually know what you're exit will be RIGHT at first. That brings me to my main point of this paragraph here, the window part that is. I don't want to give any spoilers in case you want to get the app, so I won't tell you which level it's on. On one of the levels, you have to break a window and escape through that. In other levels, you have to do things that I don't know why Hollywood would let you do, like breaking stuff. Why would they need an actor that can dive puzzles, anyway? I don't know'
The main thing that I don't like about Hollywood Escape is the fact that they have a tutorial. Wait, let me repeat that. This game has a TUTORIAL! Never have I seen a game that has a tutorial. I can understand that the director wants to talk with the player at the beginning, but he doesn't need to attend there and watch me the entire first level and help me things like, "hmm. This site is locked. Maybe there's a key hidden somewhere." Everyone who had ever played any escape game already knows EVERY hunt he gives as a tutorial person. At least he's only on the first level. This game would be good for support books who have never played a single escape game, but other that that, the tutorial is just annoying.
Well, that's all I have to say about this game. I would find it two stars, but I'm feeling nice and will give it one more since the actual puzzling in the game is moderately good for having a simple two dimensional engine. So… yeah. I remember before I got my Fire TV, I saw the trailer for this game. Then, I got a Fire TV and bought this, and it totally lived up to the hype. It is exclusive to the Fire TV, so kudos to fellow owners of it. It is a really interesting game. It is a tower defense game where you can build towers to defend the center of the map, but it's also a shooter as well. When you place your towers, you can jump into the map in person, third person to be exact, and fight alongside your levitating towers. When there's no more aliens in the part of the map you're at, or if you die, you can teleport back to the map screen and manage your towers some more by upgrading, repairing and building more of them. The program is not a freeware. So, I expected more options than what this offered.
The options are:
1) Sampling rate from 8K to 48K
2) Setting of min/max frequency
3) Manual scaling.
4) Display in log frequency.
5) Saving the graph as file.
6) Peak detect/hold.

The casual observation:
1) The screen update is about 1Hz at 16K bins.
The screen update is about 0.4 Hz at 48K bins.
2) The color of graph cannot be changed.
3) There are no averaging options such as (1/3, 1/6, etc octave smoothing).
4) Originally, I could not get this program to work on Android phone. The issue was resolved
via google search. The problem was Amazon signing issue which logged me out of the
purchased program. I send request for resolution to the developer, I have not heard
back from this issue.

Overall, it is OK program, but there are many a freeware that does more than this program.

It's not just a way to get KODI on a device, or to sideload apps, but it is a great way to organize storage. It organizes all the storage on a Fire device similar to one on a regular Android device. It is able to scan your device and SD card, to check and see if there are any repeated files, or any files not used and not needed on your device.

The app is just like the remote that comes with the Fire TV/ Fire TV stick. However, I would just stick with using the remote that came with the stick, unless you lost it or its broken. The remote is far more tactile, but the app is organized just like the remote is you need it.

I also have Pluto on my Smart TV. I was scrolling through the apps once and saw Pluto, and decided to try it out. It is set up like the guide for a big name satellite company, such as Directv or Spectrum (formally Bright House). The kindle app is slightly different, but has most of the channels that the Smart TV app had. However, this is not a replacement for cable or a main source of TV. It is only good for weather, some cartoons, health and travel, and a few gaming channels  (meaning information on video games like IGN). If you want to move off of cable or satellite due to expenses, I'd suggest you'd use this along with something like Netflix, Amazon Prime Movies and TV, or Hulu.

This claims to be a free puzzle site; however, if you enjoy playing a puzzle with more than 60 pieces, then you are out of luck here. You also have to pay in order to rotate the pieces... please, is this really a free puzzle? I think not. Don't waste your time downloading this app when there are so many truly free and, quite wonderful puzzle sites out there. Try Amazon's underground site to find free puzzle apps.

This really is the best puzzle site ever! I love the fact that it is a completely free site; that you can play a puzzle with over 400 pieces, and that they can be rotated. Just a hint for those people who enjoy the puzzle rotation mode: I noticed that the pieces will only fit together in that mode if they are correctly aligned either vertically or horizontally. This is very helpful when one is playing a puzzle with many pieces because you know which  direction certain pieces  are supposed to go once you have connected two or more of them. I also appreciate that this puzzle is truly free, as many of the puzzle boss puzzles are. They offer a great variety of free puzzles on this site as well as their other free puzzle sites. Paid puzzles are available at the beginning of the puzzle menu and they aren't obnoxious like some of the other free puzzle apps that I have seen. Personally, when a free puzzle site like this one is as courteous and as wonderful as this one is, it makes me want to consider them first when I am looking for both free, and possibly paid puzzles. I highly recommend this puzzle app!

Works like any other Kindle reading app!

The actual usage of the tool is similar to Kindle for PC and a true kindle. It's a nice way to turn your tablet into a kindle. A smartphone's screen is too small as far as I'm concerned so it should be restricted to tablets.

Edit: I have been reading complaints in the help forum about the newest version of Kindle for Android and when I got the update notice, I just said "Uh-Oh!" However, it's not that bad. Maybe I'm more flexible in what I use and how I use it but I have no serious problems with it. I'm not sure how long the new "carousel" is that you can't adjust but the latest book you're reading is clear (on top), there is a list of recent books, and it is far far easier to get to the other "pages" of the app.

You used to have to swipe to get from the "home" page to the library page regardless of whether you wanted a list of books or collections or whatever. Now, it's a simple tap at the bottom to go home, go to the library, or even to open your latest books.

Also, the collections are no longer the pre-set 3x3 display which could be very large boxes. What I see now is 4 wide but I don't remember the length. The font that shows the collection name and size is a bit small but still readable. I'm using an 11.5" diagonal tablet.

All in all -- it's fine! It's not great so I won't change my rating but I don't see the big fuss!

This plays like a simpler tiled version of "Brickshooter Egypt" by Playrix. You just slide the tiles from the center where they stop at the first possible place. The arrows on the sides tell you which rows and columns are available for sliding as well as the color. You cannot slide all the way across -- there must be a tile of some color in that row or column.

The goal is to remove all the tiles that were in the center at the beginning of the level. Those that were slid in during the level retain their arrows and if you remove a tile that allows it to move, it will. To remove any tile (or group of tiles), you must slide in to make a group of three or more contiguous tiles of the same color. Those go away when matched and any tiles with arrows shift in the direction of the arrow. This allows for the possibility of a "cascade effect" by making a group of three as it slides along.

The play is just like Brickshooter Egypt.

Plays about like all the PathPix games except instead of square cells, they are hexagonal. You just use the numbers on the cells to draw a path from one to the other. The numbers tell you how long the path is so you just match up the numbers and connect. Be careful -- there may be several with the same number nearby.

Novices may find it very complicated so I recommend you at least try the free PathPix game first to see if you understand the concepts and like the game.

I find it wonderful. With PathPix, the possible paths between two matching numbers is more limited so this is more challenging. I'm just sorry I didn't find it until today!

As complicated as PathPix Max so is really PathPix Max 2!

Definitely not for beginners or even moderate players. You really have to be an enthusiast and be prepared to take time. These puzzles are NOT designed to be done in a single setting. If you get stuck in one area, move to another area. If still stuck, go on to another puzzle and then come back. Sometimes it's just a fresh viewpoint needed.

I have all of the PathPix games and my only regret now is I just found it today. I wish I had found it when it came out!

Just as expected with any KPix game - Fantastic.

I like this game because it focuses on the image and avoids the extra (usually longer paths) to fill in the background. Unlike Art or Max, the backgrounds of most of the images are simple and by minimizing that, the game is actually more fun!

It's also geared for beginners as well as experienced "pathers" because it starts small and builds to larger and larger puzzles with longer and longer maximum path lengths.

Other than a compatibility issue, I can't see how anybody could give any of Kris's games less than a 4 star rating. They're all just that good! The game mechanics of the entire PathPix series is the same but it's still so much fun to figure out just what the image is and then the quote is the "cherry on top"!

Keep up the good work! I'm always looking for more of this series and any games by Kris. I usually snap them up as fast as I let hubby know I want it (he's a good sort, he always says yes to me :) ).

Time passed and I continued to use the Western Digital brand of Acronis and was happy, just no automatic features. Here I am on Windows 8 (64) and wanted to try it again. I bought 2 copies of the Plus version, they installed easily and backed up much quicker than Windows 8 does. I ran a full disk restore from within Windows 8 and from the F-11 boot option. No problems and a perfect restore on 2 different computers (both Win 8-64). I am one happy camper.
I now have many backups (all validated) and have them on several drives on each computer including USB drives attached to each computer ( a WD 2TB "My Book and a WD 320gb Passport). And automatic restores set for multiple schedules and days

Warning this is a powerful tool and has many options so you have to be careful, but there are tutorials for every option (READ THEM if you are not sure) Mistakes are possible, I once cloned the New Blank drive instead of my "C" drive and copied it to my "C" drive. Result you ask? Yep..a perfect clone of a blank drive :( and no more OS to clone from. Lesson learned. (READ the DRIVE ID# and Identify it is the right one..IE. WD1002FAEX)(which is my "C" drive). As far as playing well with other software I have had no problems. I also run "Norton Internet Security 2013" and "Malwarebytes Pro" on both computers, set to "aggressive" and early boot.

Do use a multi-faceted approch to backups, I backup "C" to "D", as well as "C and D" to External. That way you always have at least 2 copies of your operating system disk, on 2 different drives to restore from.
Also remember you always have "reset" on Windows 8 for a fresh 8 copy to start over. If that fails you need a win 8 disk or USB ISO Copy ( You should ALWAYS have one of those and your Key#)

The fix: open the "C" drive, Programs (X86) go to Microsoft Office then Office 14 look for EXCEL (which is listed as an application). Right click to properties click compatibility and uncheck "run as administrator" and uncheck run in "compatibility mode". at the bottom click "change for all users" and close.
Now..against advice, I put MY computer in "run in Win 7" compatibility mode" because that what we use at work. And "BINGO" Now it works great. On my wife's computer I un-checked run in compatibility mode. and it also works great.
So the main problem was "run as administrator" was checked on mine.

Final thoughts: I love it. Works great. If I were you I would buy it.

This is going to be an unsatisfactory review, because despite repeated attempts and the assistance of tech support, I was not able to get this new version of Microsoft Outlook to work with my business email server. It worked fine with the previous version of Outlook, but this time around it was a no go.

The program itself seemed okay. But one big drawback is that it appears you need to be running Office 2007 in order to get full functionality out of this program. And I don't care for Office 2007. I'm still running Office 2003 because I much prefer that suite of programs.

So mixed results for me. Not all of them are presumably the fault of the product. But ultimately this wasn't an upgrade that it felt it necessary to make.

Once you get the box the disks come in open -- which might prove to be a challenge in itself -- Vista can be a challenge for inexperienced users to install over an exiting operating system. I got it to work eventually, but it took some doing. Once it was up and running, the software worked okay, although it has its shares of annoying quirks. (But all OS do.)

Vista has been a controversial OS ever since its release. The long and short of it is: is this an improvement over Windows XP? And in my opinion, it is not. It consumes more resources than XP -- and so will likely slow most users' systems down -- but offers no substantial improvements.

As of right now, I don't see any reason to recommend that users upgrade if they're already running XP. The advantage to Vista Ultimate over the Home version of the software is that it has some additional features. But it's still not enough to make me advocate making the change.

I've been running McAfee's anti-virus software for quite a while now and am satisfied with the product. It does the job it's billed to do without causing any of the slowdown problems that other users have complained of. (Although that is always a problem when using software of this type, so caveat emptor.)

One thing I don't like is that the software installs a clunky "SecurityCenter" that I don't care for and that consumes resources. The software also wants to install a firewall (I don't care for McAfee's version), privacy software and similar. I don't like it when programs attempt to foist bloatware on users like that.

But other than that, the software operates efficiently and effectively. It does consume resources, but if you have the latest generation of PC, that shouldn't prove to be a problem.

This is easily the most comprehensive language instruction package I've ever seen. With four separate units, each split into several different sections -- including listening, speaking, vocabulary and grammar -- Rosetta Stone provides hours and hours of easy-to-use instruction in learning to speak and understand Japanese like an expert.

A language package like this requires the user to be a self-starter. There's nobody pushing you to use it or assessing your performance. The lack of feedback might prove challenging for some users. But if you're willing to push yourself, this system really works. (Of course, one advantage to this method is that you're able to move at your own pace.)

Rosetta Stone comes with a high price tag. But if you're serious about learning Japanese, and have the discipline to follow a program on your own, your purchase will be money well spent.

I gave this to a friend with a Mac to try out. He wanted to run some Windows programs on his system and agreed to give this software a go. The results were what you'd hope for: the software successfully emulated a Windows PC and allowed us to access both Windows and Mac software simultaneously. I was skeptical at first that the program would operate as claimed, but was quickly convinced. The makers of the software claim that "Windows is better on the Mac" -- and based on this program, they might just be right.

This version of Office was designed for the Mac, so in theory it should work better than the previous version. Whether or not that's the case is hard to determine, as the previous version worked well enough for most people. (I've never been convinced that all of the "upgrades" that software goes through are really improvements at all. Most of the time I prefer to just leave stuff alone.)

Some of the files can be slow to open in this version of the software, however apparently that was due to a bug, which can be corrected by updating the software to the first Service Pack release. This is a nuisance, but at least it can be corrected.

For whatever reason, Microsoft decided to strip some of the functionality from previous versions of Office for this release. Most especially, they removed the support of Visual Basic from Excel. This means that some of the features that users previously used -- like macros -- no longer work in this version of Excel. This is not something that is going to affect the basic user, but for the price, customers should be able to expect a full-featured software package.

Unlike a lot of people, I've always been an admirer of Microsoft products. Granted, they tend to be expensive, overpriced even, but they typically do what they're intended to do with a fair amount of ease. The 2008 version of Office for Mac is more of the same -- the familiar suite of office programs with some spiffed up new features -- only it suffers from the problem that causes many users to loathe Microsoft: instability. The program is generally reliable, but it still had enough problems, including an overall slowness, to be frustrating for me. I like the features, like the ease of use. But overall I kept wishing that the platform was just a little more stable.

Note that this software package is an upgrade version. You must be a licensed user of any Microsoft Office 98 Macintosh Edition suite or application, or any Office for Mac 2001-2004 suite or application.

One of the most captivating games I've ever played. Forces you to bend your mind to solve great puzzles. Played this game for about 3 months so I could form a rounded opinion. It has absolutely cute graphics and a well-executed story. Great characters; some so sweet they'll cause cavities.  The HOS' range from easy to extremely hard depending on the level, room, and existing mode (night, anomaly, reverse, etc.). The reason I only gave it 2 stars is because after you get past the early levels, it quickly becomes a thinly veiled attempt to get you to spend your real money and lots of it. As your level gets higher, you get more energy points to use BUT, simultaneously, you must use much more energy to investigate a room. The result being that you can't investigate as many rooms as when you had less max energy.  You will also notice quickly that the higher your level, the less often you find useful items after searching a room. And, the more diamonds you need to buy the items you need to either detain a criminal or complete a collection. As if that's not insulting enough, when you need to gather items for a collection or to be able to search a special place or event, you have to get an absurd number of them (like 40 of one thing). I've been playing Mystery Manor simultaneously and can definitively state that I'd rather spend my hard earned funds there than at Mirrors of Albion. At least with Mystery Manor you don't have to go broke if you don't want to have a gazillion friends or spend a ton of cash. I certainly hope Game Insight is paying attention and so are you. Am hoping that they will eventually  stop ripping us off. In the meantime, I'm putting this game on hold.

If a game developer wants to make this type of game, I'd strongly recommend they look at this one to see how it should be done. The strategy guide is easy to follow but you can follow the story without needing it. The hint "arm" is very helpful and as you go along, offers powers necessary for getting through some spots. The puzzles and HOS' are more difficult than most. They tend to be dark and in keeping with the general theme of demons and creepy things. If you don't like this type of story, don't even think about this one. And, obviously, if you like creepy, this one is worth the price of admission.

First, I'd like to tell those people who complain about having to pay to unlock the full game: Please read the description before downloading. They tell you quite clearly that "free" is a relative term in gaming. Most of the good games either will charge you for the full version OR, will charge you as you play for critical items (diamonds, energy, keys, whatever...). Don't forget they want to make a living at this and unless you want pop-up or banner ads, we have to pay something. Now G5 and a couple of others have gotten too big for their britches and charge $5 or more but that's just my opinion.

As for Mystic Diary: great game with a solid storyline and decent enough graphics. It took me slightly more than 3 hours to play through. For what is mostly a one-man project, this was very solid. I'd like to see more from him soon. Great for smaller children as there aren't any creepy monsters but some of the searches may be hard for little ones.

I do have to mention that my Kindle HDX crashed a few times during play but this seems to happen rather randomly with games. May very well be a Kindle problem. Anyone else?

It's somewhat difficult and there's no Strategy Guide which will no doubt put some players off but the Hint button is very useful. While a HOS game by description, this one uses them rather sparingly. The other puzzles are relatively easy and actually add to game play in a way that doesn't feel so much like just filler. There's quite a bit of back and forth so I would have loved to see them change the map to allow you to change location by clicking on where you want to be. Lastly, although the theme is demons, I wouldn't rule this one out for any but the really young kids. However, as always,you know your kids best and they should be supervised while on any computer. You be the one to choose what they are exposed to.

Unfortunately, it is translated into English probably from an Asian language by a non-professional translator leading to some peculiar, if not funny, comments. A huge improvement would be somewhere kind of strategy guide like some have. It's not the worst game I've come across so that's why they get 2 stars.

Incidentally, reading many of the reviews, I get the quick impression that many of the most positive ones aren't legitimate. There's a similar lack of information, similar terms and tone that make them sound staged.
