The map is interactive meaning you can &#34;teleport&#34; to any available scene - yay!  The reason for my less-than-awesome grade is that the developers have done nothing about the annoying delay returning to the scene after reading a journal entry or the map (or both bc at least you can flip from journal to map or back using tabs. The delay in returning to the scene of your choice is made more annoying by being shown the title scene every time. I also encountered a serious glitch in one of the puzzles where the menu pop-up showed after every move no matter what I pressed. Also, in some scenes, I had to try several times to perform an action required. This is by no means a difficult game in casual mode but you can choose a more difficult version. My life is stressful enough without making my games add to it! In my opinion, this one's really great for those new to HOS games or those who are looking for an interesting take on the murder mystery HOS genre - no demons, ghosts, monsters, gore. Tame enough for some older preteeners.

A wonderful opportunity for a great game that never quite fulfilled the promise. Sigh... I spent about 12 yrs of my life living about 5 miles from the town of Sleepy Hollow NY which drew my attention to this game immediately. After reading the "book jacket info" which further enticed me to not only try it but also buy the full version. The storyline is indeed very good but the execution left something to be desired. As it is, it rated a 4 star review largely because I enjoyed the presentation of the story and liked playing it. The following are the reasons why I gave it a wishy washy 4 stars.
1) my #1 or one of them anyway is that some of the HOS objects were too small to see comfortably even with my strongest glasses on. Not the actual object. Some of the HOS give you pictures of the objects you're looking for instead of the names. I play on a Kindle 7HDX & I say, bless you if you play on any smaller device. Some of the HOS objects are hidden behind other objects and some colors are different than what's on the list.
2) Hint button is only useful to find out WHERE to go next but a lot of the helps are quite vague.
3) a Strategy Guide is provided but pauses the game while you search AND, it's quite small, hard to read.
4) you can zoom a bit to improve HOS searches but the moment you tap on anything, it zooms back out.
These are just my pet peeves. Regardless of my complaints, I still think it was long and fun to play and for 2.99, a good value. I recommend it but I like to let others know clearly why I did & didn't like the game.

This isn't the first game I've played with a card game/magician as the central character. It is, however, the more unusual one of the few I've played. If you only play until the unlock screen you won't understand the relationship between the characters or why one of them is trying to stop your progress. I enjoyed this game even though I encountered a couple of minor glitches and one big one where my Kindle 7HDX actually rebooted but it did return me to exactly where I was. Go figure! There is a helper character in this one that travels with you to the end (a sort of rabbit) &, briefly, a raccoon too. Some of the cut scenes are silly and unnecessary. There's also a series of puzzle pieces for a puzzle that is a bonus content item but finding them is oddly very difficult. Many pieces only have a corner visible & despite my usual enjoyment of hunting for these bonus items, I lost interest after realizing that it was a real job finding them all. The mini-games were also tedious because most of them required too many steps. For example, we're all familiar with the game where you are shown a series of lights or musical notes and your task is to repeat each series exactly. In most games, you do this about 4 or 5 times. Here, it went on about 7. C'mon now guys! Anyway, as HOS and point & click gaming go, I think this one's a firm 4. Decent storyline and some interesting characters along the way, a scattering of HOS, a good bonus chapter, good interactive map, decent help, and a great strategy guide that's easy to access and use. Some of the graphics were really well put together too.

Above all - this remains an HOS game. Do not bother if you don't like them. It's annoying to read reviews by persons who don't like to play HOS games that are upset that it's an HOS game.

Caveat: I only played to level 5 so my opinion is limited to that experience. I don't play many casino slot games but of the ones I have played, this one ranks near the bottom though by no means the worst. First of all, I found the music really annoying after just a few minutes. That, at least, can be turned off. My gripe with the game is with the payouts.  I've been to Vegas and as cheap as I am, generally stick to the penny or nickel slots and have made $20 last way longer and won more $$ than in this virtual casino with $2000. In 5 levels I couldn't even sniff a chance to win the jackpot. If you figure that you're spending 30 coins per turn (at lowest rate) and you win 8 coins, it's sad. The biggest payout I had was ~385 coins. Even with an hourly free coin bonus, you will feel pressed to buy more coins if you really want to play on. There are much better slot games that you can play & not spend real cash to have fun. Keep on looking.

I'm not a huge player of slot games but I've tried enough to get a feel for the different approaches that developers have taken to the genre. This one is a middle of the road one for me. The reasons I don't like it are: 1) each time you get more points, the game circle window at the bottom of the page pops up to let you know that you have a new high score. And, if you don't wait long enough for it to disappear, the game circle window pops up to tell you all about your awards. It gets old fast; 2) I played up to 7 levels & was only 1.7K in points towards the 10K needed to open the next machine without paying for it in real cash. This means that if I kept on until I earned the necessary points to open the next machine, I would only have access to 2 machines for as long as that took (a Xmas themed one and an Egyptian themed one). Aaaagh! 3) but minimal is that payouts are largely slim.

So that's it. It's free to try but keep in mind that there are many great ones to choose from.

Although I ran into a few glitches early in the game, I was able to play 99% of it with no problems.

As for it being slow, the amount of time it takes to download has a lot to do with your internet connection speed. Whatever type of provider you have, you should know the Mbps. They vary from around 3 to 60 and over though it can be prohibitively expensive. I tell you this so you understand that the higher that number, the faster your games will download & run more smoothly. With newer games having near 1G of data, you can see how much your ISP speed will affect you. Also, clean out the memory on your device - move your "keepers" to the cloud so they don't clog up your memory.

OK, that was your internet lesson for today. Aside from being a huge file, Curse of the Blackwater plays like an epic adventure. There are ancient Greek gods, mayhem, opening up of seals that never should have been touched, etc, etc. I found it absorbing and fun to play. Whatever price you end up playing, it's actually worth it because aside from being a rather lengthy main story, there's a bonus chapter that could pass for a stand-alone game too. It has HOS' but the game isn't just a vehicle for them. There are other mini-games that are interesting and not overwhelming. They did include a help button which I mostly used for help with where to go next. No strategy guide that I saw, and, unfortunately, no map - but it's not as bad as it seems. The back and forth is acceptable. I feel bad that many of you experienced so many glitches that caused you to give up cause it is really worth the time.

This is the second installment in the Enigmatis series and I loved it! That's not to say there weren't problems but, for me, they are overshadowed by the rest. I couldn't even deduct a star like I normally would. 1st, let me say that this is a creepy, high intensity game not suitable for young children for those of you that are (and you should be!!!) screening games for the kids. It deals with disturbing demonic rituals & images so be forewarned even though the focus is on the adventure. Great intensity, dramatic story, appropriate music, what more could you ask? This is an expensive game but worth the cost. It is quite long and there's a bonus chapter that's also lengthy. It takes place shortly after the end of the Ghosts of Maplecreek so you kind of feel like you never left. I hate to give away game play but I'll tell you this: you'll meet our friend, the evil priest...

As for the downsides, there's no strategy guide and the help button is of limited help. Worse is that there's an interactive map that's of little use (grrrr). I did get stuck once for lack of information but I'm willing to overlook all of this and still rate it a full 5 stars. Download this one, try it out, buy it!

I've completed several puzzles now and comfortable saying that this game definitely meets my standards for a giving it a 5 star review.  Played on a Kindle HD 10, I've encountered no glitches. I also tried the different levels & am currently using the option that lets you turn the pieces which makes it more challenging whatever level you're on. I also like the ability to get all the edge pieces separately. It's what we normally do anyway, right?  The first batch of puzzles are included. This group has variety & will keep you busy for a while. But, if you want more, there are additional puzzles you can buy. Never fear, the prices are modest & the choices are varied. For 4.99 I got some 35 additional puzzles. Keep an eye out for offers. Definite download if you either want to try jigsaw puzzles or are already an experienced fan.

Only been playing a very few weeks but am entertained enough to keep playing. How much more of an ego trip can it be? You arrive on primitive stone-age earth and join a tribe where they immediately are overwhelmed by your stunning who-knows-what that you're named chief! You get to build the village to your specs and expand to conquer neighborhood after neighborhood. Awesome! Characters are funny especially when doing a &#34;deal&#34; at the bar means one sits there and gets sloshed. Hope this doesn't eventually require spending a lot of real money in the typical bait & switch tactics of so many games. I'd say give it a try if you like or think you might like an empire building game that seems to focus more on the adventure aspect than the &#34;winning&#34; aspect of games that involve battle play.

I would have liked to write this review at the end of the game but they nag you repeatedly for it so I'm writing this with the caveat that I'm only about a quarter of the way done.

The positive reviews convinced me to play this game and for the price, it wasn't going to hurt much if I didn't like it. I must admit that I really didn't like it at the beginning. However, I kept with it because I like to give all games I download a fair try before deciding. Some just start slow. It was a bit awkward working out exactly what to do even though the "help" section gives you an overview. It features different puzzle types which I am thoroughly enjoying. Some more difficult than others and some HOS'. Hard to compare this one with other games but the premise is straightforward. Find the broken pieces of the kingdom's precious gem and save the princess from having to marry a fiend. Graphics and movement are lower tech than most "big" company (wink-wink) offerings but it's still a well put together piece. Love the music & voiceovers. Worth a try for something different.

This is in the &#34;evil demon&#34; genre but doesn't have the much of the intrigue or detail of many others I've played. At the end you are left with one particularly gaping loose end: right from the beginning you're introduced to a shadowy figure with some unusual powers. Shortly after meeting her we never hear from or about her again. Waaaahh?  The majority of the game takes place in a house which narrows the interest somewhat. Some other objectives and their resultant mini-games or HOs are sometimes mind-numbing. But it has enough going on to be interesting to make it worth checking out but only if you can get it &#34;on sale&#34; or at least a reduced rate. 4.99 is simply too much for this. Not exactly Artifex-Mundi's best effort but you might like it.

I'd like to start by noting that although this is technically the 3rd in a series, it's not really a sequel. Each of the 3 "Nightmare" games has an unique storyline and they don't tack on to each other. However, it does seem to feature the same beleaguered mother and daughter who can't seem to get rid of this ghost. Alas, we all have our problems I guess (ha ha ha). I'd also like to point out to all those new to these games: NO, they ARE NOT free. You get to play a few chapters for free to see if you like it enough to pay for the rest. As far as I've seen, all of the info sections mention that the game features in-app purchasing and many go as far as saying you will have to buy the rest of the game. My only gripe is that I want to know up front how much the full game will cost. Hello? Amazon? You listening?

As for the actual game play, this one was fun, sometimes funny, well done. I liked that it had its own storyline even though mom and daughter get kidnapped again. Also found the Bonus Chapter well done. If you enjoyed a previous "Nightmare" game, I think you'll enjoy this one. Good graphics and dialogue. Played without problems on my HDX7. It is a big file as are all newer games. Better graphics mean bigger files. If it takes you very long to load, it's probably your internet service. I use cable internet at approx 30Mbps so it only takes about 5 mins. If your ISP runs at 6Mbps, well, go get a cup of coffee/tea ,& read something while you wait....

Plays well, no glitches that I've run into after several months of occasional play.  Good choices of slots. The more you play (or spend...) you amass points that let you open new slots. However, a recent update lets you play new ones even if on a temporary basis. It doesn't take as long to level up to new slots like similar apps I've tried.  Helps to spend some real money but I did manage to play for quite a while without doing it. There are benefits to buying coins with their rewards system. This one also awards coins every 4 hours plus a wheel spin after collecting several of the other coin awards. Go ahead and try it!

(Played on Kindle HDX7)
Just finished this game including the Bonus chapter. For me, it ran somewhere around 5.5hrs.. (not in one sitting). It's your stereotypical good v evil story but more cleverly done than I was expecting. Art figures heavily in this story and I'm a sucker for all things "arty"! Yet, I was even fooled a couple of times thinking I had it all figured out. The story is about a young man who, 20 yrs earlier watched his brother disappear into a strange mist. He's been waiting for it to return and finally gets his chance to go after his brother. Initially there's a third character introduced that I felt could have been used more prominently especially in the bonus chapter but, oh well, I don't write 'em - I only get to criticize!

To those who don't like HOS, avoid this one as there are many. (They are of easy to medium difficulty.) Liked the graphics and background music though my habit is to set the music to a lower volume. There's an interactive map and great hint button too. I bought this on sale for 2.99 and feel I got a decent value. Realistically, there are only so many themes game developers can use so it's more about the creative ways in which the are presented. I thought this one was done well.

(Played on Kindle HDX7)
I'm very fond of most AM games so I usually buy them and am rarely unhappy. This would have been no exception but it didn't take long to want to slap whoever thought the voiceovers were ready for publication. The actual gameplay was mostly interesting. It tries to pick up where the 1st Dreamatorium left off but takes a different direction. The gist is that you are now looking for the crystals to open the dreamatorium because Graves' ghost is holding 3 people hostage until you do. Aside from my rant over voiceovers (see below), I was also disappointed over the stunted ending. You do all this work to get into the dreamatorium only to have a quick and unsatisfying ending. I'd say more but don't want to spoil it totally for you.

I wouldn't call the graphics 1st rate but they weren't terrible either. It definitely has a 1920's feel although some of the locks and gadgets are 21st century. No big deal. The big deal is definitely the voiceovers. All of them are flat; lacking in inflection, emotion. Very monotone even at moments where you expect a bit of startle or fear etc. AM can do much better than this. It does affect gameplay because it's part of the atmosphere. Just be warned. Definitely play the free portion before deciding on this one.

(Played on older Kindle HDX 7)
This is a long playing game and bonus chapter so while I won't exactly call it worth 4.99, it's not a terrible value even at that price. Definitely worth a the sale prices many of these developers are offering lately. I did encounter a few annoying problems but am not sure it's me or others did too. For one, some objects in the HOS list were unfamiliar to me and I'm quite good at vocabulary. Either these words are out-of-use terms for these objects or something got lost in the translation. Also, some scenes were a bit hard to pick out the objects. Sorry, I didn't write those words down as I should have but by tapping around, you can figure it out! The other annoyance was the instructions to some of the non-HOS puzzles. They aren't all inherently obvious and with a couple of them I was spending way too much time trying to figure out what they meant. Also, there's a flower puzzle where you have to rearrange the positions of the different colored flowers but no matter how I tapped the circles, all they did was go around in the same circle and positions as they started. Not even the guide was helpful here. Thank goodness for SKIP!!! The guide is otherwise excellent, the hyper-travel map is good and hint button is actually helpful. All the things you want for these adventures. By the way, keep in mind that every scene including the bonus chapter has a hidden snowglobe to find. Some are actually hidden in or behind other objects so take a moment to look if this additional feature matters to you. Besides the snowglobes, there's a 2nd "collection item" in these scenes. I've no idea why other than like the snowglobes, it's an extra thing to find. They're all different objects and many of these are cleverly (or not) hidden and are not obvious. Happy hunting! As for the main gameplay, it's hard to say more than the info already given without giving stuff away. I enjoyed this and would recommend to others as long as you're aware of the above "hiccups".

I'm quite done playing this game. I'm in the 2nd "section" - the town of Eastmire, and am stuck in the same spot as the 1st time. Like the others, I'm angry about this. I can't imagine how a game from this developer can go to market with these glaring issues. And YES, I deleted it from both my device and the cloud AND rebooted my Kindle before redownloading the game. Result: exactly the same. If you're interested in this game, bypass it until you see an update after this date that adresses the problems described by me and others!

Just finished the main game and the bonus (Kindle Fire HDX7) and though the game features some really nice graphics and great hint button, it's very short and by no means worth the 4.99 I paid.  Both parts are short!  If you can get this forr 2.99 or less, buy it. My main gripe, other than the price and length, is that in the main portion, the storyline feels forced and obvious. The bonus storyline is much better but much too short as well. I didn't see any interactive map but it wasn't necessary.  Even with the "try me" portion it plays way too short for the money.

Lost Lands is one of a few series I recommend in its entirety. They feature all the helpful extras we love like a great teleport map, very useful HELP along with the great graphics, characters, and storyline. These have  beautifully done to a high level. They are very long and include a long bonus chapter that makes the price much more palatable. As ever, be sure to try the sample (free) portion before paying for the full game. The free portion is definitely long enough to give you a sense of whether this one's for you. By the way, I had no glitches on my trusty Kindle HDX 7 (3rd gen). Enjoy!

The entire series is haunting, creepy, nightmarish. Excellent work guys!  This game, like its brethren, is stunningly well-done. Everything works fine (played on my reliable HDX7). I usually don't set any game to anything other than Casual and this was no exception. I don't play for stress so I like to have the help when I want it. This game can be difficult at times as are some of the minigames. However, I don't see this as a problem but if you're not acquainted with Ravenhearst, be prepared for this. The series works best if you start at the beginning. This chapter takes place after the events of the others so it helps to have played the others in order to follow the theme although it can and does do well as a stand-alone. Keep in mind that this is more a psychological thriller than outright murder and mayhem. It is most definitely NOT FOR YOUNG CHILDREN.  Play the free portion if you can cause it's not everyone's cup of tea.

This is an offer for potential subscribers: 30 day free trial after which you get charged in accordance to the available rates.  Do not be fooled!  The 1 star is for the bait & switch tactic. It's totally unnecessary.  As for the Post itself, I've read it many times before. It leans fairly heavily towards the sensationalist and I wouldn't exactly call it in-depth reporting though they manage to cover all the major headlines.  Oh, they do love their gossip!  Read several other reviews and make an informed decision.

Funny zombie-based adventure!  Fun to play but in order to make progress at any reasonable rate requires spending your real, hard-earned cash for things like "brains" in order to complete tasks. Still, it's addictive and fun.

Been playing for a few weeks now and am enjoying the entertainment. Wether you need to fill a few minutes or a lot, this is a fun casino game compared to several others I've tried. They start you with a generous amount of chips that I found can actually grow or at least not disappear so fast!  You just have to be conservative with betting at the beginning. Also like that they offer good deals to buy more chips so you can keep playing and not break the bank. Hint: Keep an eye on the daily offers for the best deals.

I found this one to be squarely in the "Meh" column.  Some beautiful graphics, some just dark and seemingly unnecessary. Storyline has potential but I agree that it felt rushed. For me, the ending was a bit of a disappointment.  My main gripe is that it was neither really spooky nor light-hearted. A very middle of the road piece.

This HOS game has all the best attributes. To me, the most important of these attributes is when the storyline works cohesively with the gameplay. Nothing angers me when developers turn out a game where the story is just a thinly veiled attempt at trying to tie together a bunch of HOS and a scattering of mini games. This game does an excellent job of tying everything together. It also has all the extras we've gotten used to having to help us along with the journey (transportation map with marks showing where you have things to do, help button, skip button for when needed). There is no guide but I didn't miss it although I usually leave the games on casual mode so it's at my pace at all times. It's also a good continuation of this series.  Definitely recommend this one.  (Played on 2nd gen Kindle fire.)

I had started this game quite a while back but was very new to games so found it way over my head. Just reopened it to play and glad I did!  It is challenging but not ridiculously hard. The hardest part for me was remembering where all the parts belonged as there are nearly 70 scenes. The hint button is very useful for finding your way without giving any more information beyond location. If you are really stuck you can open a brief help video from the hint screen. The addition of a teleportation map is a huge help because of the many scenes and nonlinear nature of the layout. It doesn't send you to every scene but will get you close enough so it's not far. This game is NOT a hidden object game. You are searching for a lost treasure that requires you to pick up objects to open locations and solve riddles. You also use a camera to take photos to help you solve other puzzles. This game requires patience and problem solving techniques. Still, a very enjoyable and well done adventure.

I stumbled onto this gem of a game and am so very glad I did. I agree with the many 4 and 5 star reviews: this is well-executed in every important aspect like great graphics, captivating story, help for when you need it.  Yes, an interactive map would be a welcome addition. The best part is the price - $1.99.  At a time when Artifex Mundi is trying to make us believe that they can only put out great games if they charge us $7, this developer manages a top tier adventure for so much less. Considering that even with the longest of games it's possible to finish in one day, it adds up VERY quickly!

This is my third SpecialBit game and I highly recommend all of them. For a very small studio, they sure put out a product that stands out for being well-done on every level especially when we are being bombarded by so many very "meh" games from the big players. This one combines a bit of live action acting with more traditional backgrounds and puzzle play. The puzzles require thought and problem solving and definitely rank among some of the harder ones I've played. I admit to having to skip a few that I couldn't work out what to do. But then again, I'm clearly better at some puzzles than others. Great story, romantic and somewhat unexpected ending.  Great help button. No map but you don't really need it as its put together in sections that don't carry over into one another.

(Played on Kindle hdx7 fire)
This game started out really well. It does a good plot, graphics, interactions. Plus, you get the interactive map, help, and guide. Not sure how far into this one I was but long enough to have paid for the full version. I started having problems with freezing. At first I thought it was just that one frame but after restarting the game several times, I got around it for the moment only to have it freeze again at another frame. After another freeze, I was back at the fireplace scene and - froze again. I'm done with this until I see an update to address the problem! You'd think that a problem this obvious would have been caught and corrected during quality assurance/testing. Please get this fixed Big Fish; I like this game and series.

Great game!  Just finished this game and found it really well done beginning to end. I didn't encounter any glitches so hopefully, the ones described by others have been addressed fully. The protagonist (you) are trying to find your sister at a haunted hotel where a vengeful ghost has already killed several people. While there, you also meet a little girl that got lost and is now caught up in this nightmare. There are lots of different types of mimi-games and HOS'. Though, if I had one complaint, perhaps it's the abundance of mini-games as some scenes have them back to back. That's what a SKIP button is for, I guess...  Great scenery, spooky scenes, eerie music, even some jump scares!  As always, play the free part before agreeing to the 4.99 price. Not everything is for everyone.

The storyline is pretty good. The reason I'm on the fence on this one is that I found quite a bit of the graphics to be mediocre. Especially the people which I found in some cases to be almost laughable. I'd recommend playing the free portion first as I do with all games but, in my opinion, this one's not worth $5. Try to get it on sale.

One of the best games to come out recently! Excellent graphics, characters, music, etc. Well-developed story with several twists and turns throughout. A lot of attention to detail in every aspect of this game except perhaps the map which seemed out of character with how well done the rest of the game is. It gave multiple messages saying I couldn't transport to a site I needed to be at. It's not much trouble since the chapters are arranged such that areas are grouped together. No matter, this game and the bonus chapter is top-notch. Start with the free portion and go for it.

Reliably great graphics and an entertaining storyline with a good set of plot turns.  The interactive map is helpful but not always right. It may say you have a task when there's nothing to do. It doesn't really matter because this game is essentially divided into sections so you're not travelling too far at any given point. There are few HOS' but be prepared cause some pieces are difficult. Good minigames too.  I found the Bonus Game to be rather mediocre and like something the developer felt like they had to be put in. It's a flashback. Still, a good, entertaining game.

As a teacher, I thoroughly enjoy apps and games that allow children to learn while having fun. The kids of today are naturally drawn to technology and anything on a screen instantly becomes ten times more exciting. Many schools and educational daycare centers even use technology like tablets and computers to teach children. This app does a wonderful job of building the fundamentals young children need to succeed in school. The best part? Parents and caregivers don't need to do much besides download the app and help their children navigate it. It's designed to be easy for small children to use and parents to customize.

Abby Monkey becomes an instant friend and teacher for young children. The app's bright, colorful hues and upbeat sound effects will delight young children. Kids will smile as they watch Abby ride across the screen in her train, ready to lead them to a learning adventure! The menu is very kid-friendly and uses basic symbols to indicate the different types of games. Games are simple to play using intuitive touch and drag motions that little hands can easily complete. Correct answers are rewarded with a monkey smile and 'toot toot' from the train whistle while a gentle thumbs-down indicates a wrong answer. Players can try again as many times as they'd like which reduces any possible frustration and encourages children to keep trying.

After finishing a set of activities in a group, children are rewarded with a fun virtual sticker that they can place on a virtual display. They also have opportunities to drag-and-drop train cars to customize Abby Monkey's train. There are tons of fun and educational activities to keep kids interested.

This app will provide hours of entertainment for children as they work through 14 different activities. The activities cover various building blocks of early education including shapes, numbers, letters, patterns, grouping, colors, and matching. Games are grouped by skill so that children can work on specific skill sets one at a time. Every game features wonderful full color images and delightful voice overs and sound effects. The app overall is very professionally done, especially when you consider its low price. These activities are enjoyable for children, and they also follow the content curriculum of grades preschool-K. Preparation aids a child's success in school in obvious ways, and this app is a fun way to accomplish basic educational goals.

I am very impressed with this app. It is sure to be a hit among kids. Abby Monkey is an enjoyable character, and the app runs very smoothly and quickly. Menus and settings make customization easy, and parents can easily enjoy teaching their children with this fun app.

Reading skills are vital in all areas of a child's schooling and everyday activities. It is also an area many, many learners struggle with at some point. In order to become a proficient reader, young learners need to start at the basics. This means that one of the best ways parents can prepare their children for reading instruction is teaching them the alphabet and basic words.

This sounds easy enough, but alphabet instruction can quickly become boring or repetitive beyond the traditional alphabet song and common activities like playing with magnetic letters on the fridge. Learners can quickly become disinterested with no way to gain more skill. Letter Quiz Aquarium School Adventure provides fresh activities that help children learn the alphabet and basic skills while having a blast. They will delight in the app's seven unique alphabet activities and build confidence as their knowledge increases. The app is simple to use and so intuitive that even small children can play with it unassisted.

The activities range from listening to the alphabet song to more complex letter ordering and timed challenges. Flashcards provide multiple formats and examples for children to learn with. Simply just clicking through them can be very beneficial. Pictures and fun voice effects reinforce letter sounds and words, helping learners of all types to grasp concepts. Children can also match lowercase and uppercase letters, match objects to their beginning sounds, and take a letter quiz to test their skills. There's even a connect the dots game where children must order letters correctly to reveal a fun picture. The app certainly provides some really creative activities to hold your child's interest and keep them playing for hours.

The app is very customizable as well. Children can make choices such as what style of flashcards they would like to play with and the patterns and colors their letters come in during certain games. Some activities even have built in difficulty levels, allowing users to adjust as they learn more. A settings menu for adults provides numerous options including the order letters are presented, the inclusion of upper or lowercase letters, and time limits for timed challenges. For $1.99, this app will go far since the difficulty can adapt to even experienced learners. Both beginners and alphabet pros will have fun with this app.

Rounds of applause and fun voices await your child when they successfully finish an activity. Mistakes are no problem and quickly correctable. Children will be encouraged to try again, and they will never feel overwhelmed or pressured while playing these upbeat alphabet games. Everyone is truly a winner and can benefit greatly from the alphabet knowledge the app provides.

An easy to use menu, fun fishy creatures, and friendly, professional voice effects make this app an excellent choice for young learners. As a teacher, I know that one of the best things you can do to aid early reading instruction is get children accustomed to recognizing letters and letter sounds. After all, letters and sound units are the building blocks of our language. Couple this fun app with reading to your child and positive encouragement, and you're well on your way to supporting a great reader.

Children love to play, but wouldn't it be nice to provide them with something educational while they're having fun? Parents no longer need to fight with their children over video game time with Abby Monkey in the scene! Video games may seem like time-wasting fluff, but many games can give your young child a boost and head start in education. As an educator myself, I recognize the value in learning through play. Children won't even know they're learning and gaining skills while completing their favorite activities. That is truly the beauty in apps such as this one.

Abby Monkey Basic Skills Vol. 1 provides a suite of fun games for preschoolers and kindergarteners. Each and every activity is specially designed to target a basic skill children will encounter during their first years of school. The application contains 12 exciting activities. The skills covered align with the academic content standards teachers use to design instruction. These activities include learning the alphabet, counting, recognizing shapes, colors, matching and patterns, pairing and finding differences, ordering, and puzzles that promote logical thinking. Beginners will be able to pick up quickly on the simple games, and seasoned learners will enjoy repeat visits to their favorite learning activities.

Abby Monkey is a friendly companion who rewards correct answers with excited voice effects and positive gestures. This positive reinforcement keeps kids encouraged and interested. If a wrong answer is selected, no problem- a gentle thumbs down and encouragement to try again is all Abby Monkey needs to let children know it's okay to make mistakes. Once finished with an activity, children can celebrate a job well done by selecting a special sticker for a virtual album. They can even have fun designing Abby Monkey's train and see her ride in it across the home screen! This customization makes children feel like they are in charge and provides motivation to keep playing. Throw in bright, enticing colors, fun cartoon images, and professional voice overs, and you have the ingredients for the fantastic learning app that Abby Monkey proves itself to be!

The app runs beautifully on a smartphone or Kindle, making it the perfect activity to keep your little ones occupied during appointments and errands. The intuitive design includes an easily accessible menu which allows the user to tap symbols to play the various included games. Children will be able to build motor skills as they tap, drag, and select answers. There is even a settings menu adults can use to customize what kind of games and hints children have access to. This makes the app very adaptable to all needs and allows children to focus on specific skills or only play their favorite games.

For the low price of $1.99, this app is well worth it for the educational benefits it provides. The fun variety of games and extra activities is sure to keep kids occupied for hours while giving them a jump start in school.

I've thoroughly reviewed the full app and can't recommend it enough, but I thought I'd drop a few words on the lite version as well so people know what they're getting with this app. For those who are unaware, sight words are words that commonly appear in reading but don't always follow standard phonics rules. For this reason, they need to be memorized through practice and educational activities, as well as reading texts that include them. This app and its full version do this beautifully. Right away, players can experience the brightly-colored designs and backgrounds, friendly space characters, and professional, upbeat voice overs.

This version is a nice intro to just try out a couple of the games. Players can still create their own avatar, and kids love this. You can choose to create a girl, boy, or even a monster. The parts are interchangeable and can create some very silly outcomes. You can still access the records sections to view scores for what is unlocked. Word lists are from the Dolch sight words lists and can be viewed by tapping the cog on the home screen of the app. Peruse this and you will probably see the same words your children are learning in school each day. These words are used in the games and sorted by difficulty, pre-k-grade 3. There is also a list of nouns.

The two games that are unlocked in the lite version are sure to entertain while they educate. The first game, word machine, says a word aloud and displays 3 options to select the correct word from. Correct answers are awarded points, with more points given for quicker answers. Gears is similar in that payers are given a word aloud and must choose the written version that matches. Players drag the cog with the correct word to its spot on the machine. Verbal encouragement is provided by the fun voices of the app's characters while wrong answers are not a big deal. Even those who are easily frustrated can enjoy these games and learn without feeling pressured.

The other games, bingo, memory, and spelling, are only in the full version. These are what you would expect pretty much. Bingo involves a bingo card players fill in by matching written words to the ones said. Memory has players memorize a word's position and select it from memory as it is called. Spelling is a great tool where players simply drag letters to spell the words. This makes the app extra worth it if your child has trouble spelling, as hearing the words and learning to recognize patterns can really benefit them.

There are also digital flashcards. In my opinion, the flashcards alone are worth the price tag. The words are displayed against a fun space background with little characters popping in from time to time. When tapped, the word on the card is said aloud, so even beginners can play and quiz themselves alone. This is something paper flashcards just can't do. The flashcards can entertain kids for quite some time on their own. I work as a tutor and, surprisingly, students of all ages report back that flashcards help them and they enjoy them. This is just a more modern and fun take on the traditional flashcards we've all used.

Overall, it's a great app for boosting reading skills. Get the lite version, see if you enjoy the games, and upgrade if you enjoy the overall feel of it. Keep in mind the game may seem too easy in this version because only pre-k is playable- the other difficulties available in the full version may suit your needs better.

I love Abby Monkey and her apps. Abby Monkey is just such a fun character and kids will love her. Better than kids just loving it, this app includes activities that are based off proven learning methods.

The Montessori method of phonics moves away from learning the traditional ABC song and toward actually learning the sounds the letters make. These sounds are the building blocks of phonics, and this knowledge empowers young learners to move on to more difficult reading. Each sound is reinforced through seeing it in print, hearing it aloud, and connecting it to words. Building connections through various means is the key to learning, and this app understands that.

The game involves various levels that become unlocked as the previous ones are completed. Each level involves a set of letter sounds. This ensures players master letter sets one at a time before moving on, so they are sure to learn the entire alphabet of sounds. Each level includes 6 phases of matching games. The player has to match letters/sounds in a memory game, and then they get to identify animal names that begin with a certain sound. Animals are dragged into Abby's train car. As the player moves through the phases of each level, more animals and sounds must be selected correctly.

By focusing on letter sounds, how they're written, and how they sound in words, this app creates connections that make concepts easy to memorize. The tactile component of moving things on the screen and tapping aids learning in many individuals, and kids will remain engaged throughout this app's fun tasks. After completing part of a level, players get to collect a fun sticker and place it on a virtual board. I do wish this game included the customization of Abby's train like in previous apps, but this is a minor wish and doesn't take away from the educational aspects.

Kids will love the bright colors of this app. There are dozens of fun, happy animals throughout and the stickers are animal themed as well. Kids tend to love animals, so the engagement factor is definitely there. They are sure to feel great as they learn how to pronounce the names of their favorite animals. Both phonics beginners and more experienced learners can enjoy these games. As a tutor, I have used these methods even with older students who have reading difficulties. Sometimes you just have to go back to the basics, and this app makes it enjoyable. In fact, kids don't even realize they're learning because it's a game!

Between the encouraging professional voices, enticing illustrations, and smooth, exciting games, Abby Monkey Phonics is the perfect way to learn these crucial skills. I think this app is well worth the low price tag, and hours of educational entertainment are bound to ensue. Whether your little one is just starting to learn to read or they have fallen behind, Abby Monkey is there to assist with a smile on her face and a train to adventure.

As reading is the skill that leads to learning most other content and skills, we spend a lot of time teaching our children about letters, sounds, and words. Young children can benefit greatly and prepare for the future by learning about letters and their associations with words. The best type of learning for very young children is conducted through play, as that is how they discover the world. Apps like 'ABC Alphabet Aquarium School' are ideal for this purpose.

The app's producer, 22Learn, makes a variety of learning apps for kids. Many of these deal specifically with phonics, letters, and other concepts that help children develop reading skills as they play. I use their apps often with my students (I work as a teacher/tutor) and they are generally well-received. I love their apps because they are backed by educational professionals, research, and methods real teachers use in schools everyday. These apps make it easy and fun to learn- providing the added value of entertainment and keeping kids busy- so children can get a 'head start' and build the vital skills they need to succeed in school.

This app is great for beginning learners because it goes through each letter individually. This allows children to learn them one at a time and move on when they have mastered the previous letter. Each letter of the alphabet includes four activities- a letter puzzle, a puzzle that associates the letter with a word that contains the letter as its initial sound, a drag and drop activity with more initial-sound associations, and, finally, a matching/shape recognition activity using the letter and even more word associations. By presenting the letter, saying it aloud (the app contains spectacular professional voice acting!), and showing how it is used in words, the app builds connections in the player's brain, creating a lasting impression of the concept that they can build off of.

Once one letter is mastered, the next letter appears with the four activities customized to that letter. The first activity- the letter puzzle- helps build recognition of the letter and is especially useful to tactile learners as they 'build' the shape by selecting pieces. Children will especially love the next activity which involves building animals with names that begin with the letter they are studying! It is a very unique and cute activity. The last two activities are drag-and-drop puzzles which are friendly for young hands (it does not have to be 'perfect' to snap into place for a correct answer- none of my young students have had an issue with that), and learners can only benefit from hearing more words and examples. Tapping a letter prompts an upbeat voice to pronounce the word, which is fantastic!

During this seaside adventure, encouraging voices and entertaining, child-friendly characters provide motivation through professional voice acting and illustrations. The app has a seaside theme kids are sure to enjoy, and the bright colors are inviting and keep kids entertained for hours. Professional voices pronounce the letters accurately, so there is no worry about children learning incorrect sounds. A comprehensive settings menu allows for turning off certain activities, sound, and music, as well as erasing game progress. Children can play what they like and practice only what they need to master if they wish.

Overall, 22Learn knocked it out of the park! For the low price, this app is definitely worth the hours of learning and entertainment it provides. Professional illustrations and voicing give it an edge over competing apps, and it is backed by educational methods that are effective. If your young child is interested in the alphabet and you're looking for a fun, unique way to teach them- this app is it!

I decided to write this review because I bought the full app and loved it. I saw a lot of confusion in the reviews about the lite version (this product) and wanted to give a better insight as to what the app offers and does. It is a lite version, but it still contains enjoyable games and does a great job of showing potential buyers what they get in the full version.

Alphabet Aquarium is an app that is designed to help young learners master the alphabet through playing fun games. The app presets one letter at a time, and letters may be chosen freely from the menu or played in order. Each letter contains four activities tailored to that letter/sound, and completing all four correctly prompts the app to move on to the next letter and its activities. So whether you have a beginning learner or an alphabet wizard, they will always have something to do that fits what letters they want to learn, practice, and master. Settings also allow certain activities to be turned off, as well as sounds and music, so it is highly customizable for your child's needs. If your little learner happens to master all 26 letters, no problem- a tap of a button erases progress and allows players to start a brand new alphabet adventure.

The first game, Letters Puzzle,involves selecting pieces of the current letter and fitting them to the letter's form. This is great for learners who learn better through doing hands-on things (this is a large amount of learners, and all young children benefit from motor activities) and helps build connections between the letter's form, its sound, and how it's used. The second activity, Animals Puzzle, involves building an animal with a name that begins with the letter being studied. Children love animals and learning what letters their favorites start with is empowering and fun. Children will soon forget they're learning and get lost in this seaside letter paradise!

The third and fourth activities- Sky and Beach Puzzle- introduce players to even more letter-word associations. By making these connections, children are actually learning the basics of reading and will grasp phonics and word formation more easily with practice. Since the alphabet is the very core of phonics and reading, these games are highly educational and outstanding features of the app. Players match words beginning with the current letter to their outlined form (it works on shape recognition skills as well, as an added bonus!). Words are written below each shape with the current letter highlighted. Tapping the words prompts the app to say them aloud with fantastic, professional voice overs. It is clear that the app builds connections for young learners, and I wouldn't be surprised if your young one is excitedly sharing all the new words he or she is learning!

As a teacher, I love apps like these because they hit all the modalities of learning- visual, hands-on, and auditory. There is no better way to build connections than through engaging practice activities- much like the ones this app offers! Since the app is produced using professional educational methods, I feel good about choosing this app for my young learners over other options that do not consider professional methods of learning. The app's fun sea theme, professional, encouraging voice overs, and colorful illustrations are sure to make it an instant favorite. I would recommend trying it out for the unlocked letters (A-E) and unlocking the full version if it's a hit. The quality is apparent on first use and the activities are sure to boost letter recognition and learning.

I LOVE this app's full version so I just had to stop by and explain what a terrific learning app it is. The sample doesn't do this app justice because the amount of content it contains is so massive, but it does do a good job giving an idea of what to expect in the full app. This app features a very fun bubble-popping theme, cute illustrations, professional voice overs, and a variety of proven educational activities back by professionals in the field. As a teacher, my students love using 22Learn apps and they are generally of exceptional quality-well worth the low price and a great value when compared to similar apps at this price point that offer much less.

The sheer amount of topics covered is astounding and sure to keep even the most avid learners busy for awhile. Upper and lowercase letters, numbers, colors, shapes, toys, farm and zoo animals, fruits, and vegetables are all covered and each has their own activities. In fact, there are three activities for each concept- "Let's Learn", "Let's Play", and "Bubble Pop!"

"Let's Learn" gives a small, fun lesson to the user by displaying objects, showing their written names, and saying them out loud. A picture of each new thing is placed in a bubble. Tapping the bubble provides a satisfying "pop!" sound and prompts a friendly, professional voice to say the word once again. This can be repeated as many times as the player chooses- the next word isn't displayed until the user taps the left or right arrows on the sides of the screen. This is great for learning at an individual pace, and repetition builds connections and keeps information locked into the brain. It is so easy and fun to learn this way!

"Let's Play" allows users to test their skills. Users can even select a cute and cuddly animal avatar to accompany them on their bubble-popping adventure! The game contains various levels. At level one, a word is said and a picture displayed. Users must tap and pop the bubble that contains the thing that was called. As correct bubbles are popped, points are awarded and the difficulty increases, providing more options to choose the correct answer from. Players are encouraged through rounds of applause, friendly characters and encouraging sound effects all wrapped in a friendly, low-pressure learning environment. It is very fun and users can even check and best their high scores from a menu accessible on the home screen.

"Bubble Pop" is the third mode and is a "free play" experience. Bubbles in the selected category float up the screen and users pop them. When popped, the name of the object inside is called out. This provides even more repetition and is a great mode for just winding down and popping away. Learning in a fun fashion is what this app does best, and this mode is just icing on the cake!

The free version includes all the activities, but only three categories-farm animals, colors, and lowercase letters- unlocked. If you try the app and like the bubble-popping fun activities, I would recommend the full version. It's well done, professionally voiced and illustrated, and backed by effective educational methods. The amount of content and customizable settings ensure this app will satisfy for a long time.

Kid's Vehicles 1: Fire Truck is a great app for children who are interested in vehicles or emergency response. This app has very nice three-dimensional graphics and features a professionally-voiced, friendly firefighter who is ready to educate the player about the firetruck and guide the adventure! Whether a free-play exploring experience or entertaining objective-based game is what you're after, children are sure to enjoy this app and remain entertained while they learn about firetrucks.

Vehicles are very popular among children, and your little one may even be interested in a future career in public safety. Apps like these are a great way to pique and encourage their interests. The app is extremely detailed and even as an adult I learned a lot about firetrucks and what kinds of tools firefighters use. I would expect no less from 22Learn, as their apps are usually of exceptional quality and well-designed to encourage learning through play.

The game includes four game modes which are unique enough to keep little ones entertained for hours. The first game mode features an interactive firetruck. Users can tap parts of the firetruck to turn on the sirens and lights, lift the ladder, open doors and shutters, and listen to voice effects on the radio or from the firefighter. Once shutters are lifted, users can tap the tools inside to learn their names. There is a wide variety of tools to learn about. Users can tap arrows at the bottom to get a better view of other sides of the truck and learn about even more tools firefighters use. For each tool tapped and each action completed, the firefighter says the names and actions in a friendly, professional voice. There is certainly plenty to learn about!

The second mode lets users drive the truck. It offers a view of the dashboard complete with interactive buttons. This mode is really awesome because it accesses your rear-view camera so children can use their imagination to guide drives around their house or wherever they happen to be. Tilting the device turns the wheel and activates the appropriate turn signal. Other buttons allow users to hear a voice over the emergency radio, honk the horn, turn the ignition, play with the radio, turn on a simulated GPS and voice navigation, toggle sirens and lights, and clean the windshield. Occasionally, dirt will splat on the windshield and require a cleaning from the windshield wipers. Very fun mode that makes kids feel like real firefighters who are driving a firetruck!

The third and fourth modes are simple for young learners and quite fun. In firefighting mode, players respond to building fires. Fires appear on the building and users must tap to put them out. If too many fires are missed, 'extra help' arrives and the game ends, but users can try again and the game encourages the player to do so. In item finder mode, users must pan around the truck and click on the object that appears. This is a great way to learn the parts and tools as well as test knowledge and memory.

Settings allow users to toggle hints and the obstacles in driving mode as well as music, sound, and device tilt response. There is plenty of help if users are stuck through instructions and hints. The app is sure to entertain with its fun graphics, multitude of activities and things to learn, and friendly voice overs. If there's a little firefighter or vehicle enthusiast in your house, this app is well worth the low price!

I reviewed the full version of this app and decided to write here as well so users get a better idea of what they are buying and its quality. First of all, I love 22Learn apps in general and this app is a great addition to their collection. It is backed by real professional education methods and activities that have been proven to improve motor skills. The puzzles are mostly shape recognition, but there are some nice mini-game type of activities for kids to enjoy.

As you would expect, the free version is just the paid version with some of the activities locked. Just like the paid version, the user is greeted with a visually appealing storybook-themed menu screen. Sliding a button allows the user to navigate to the activities menu. Since there are no buttons, this app is very friendly for little hands and most children will be able to play on their own. The professional voice overs are enjoyable and give the user a taste of the sound effects available in the full app.

Two of eight of the activities are unlocked in the free version, which isn't too bad. The first unlocked app is the farm animal shape recognition activity. Users drag the animal shape into its appropriate slot. The user can then view a fun animation of the animal and hear some related sound effects. The other animal puzzle and the vehicle puzzles are very similar to this activity, so children will probably like the app very much if they enjoyed the animal activity. The other unlocked activity is the build-a-xylophone shape recognition game. Users drag sections of the xylophone to their appropriate slots. After building is complete, users can tap sections of the xylophone to play notes and create their own tunes. This is my favorite activity out of all eight, and I feel that kids will enjoy it a lot as well.

The only activities not really represented in the free version are the build-a-popsicle and flower growing activities. In those, children drag and drop pieces into slots to create their own popsicles. The flower activity involves dragging pots and clouds into position in order to grow a flower. After building is complete, users can tap completed ice creams and flower pots to watch animations and hear sounds again.

If you enjoy the sample activities, it is likely the paid version will be worth it for you and your little one. There is a nice mix of activities that are designed to build motor skills. Parents will love how this app holds a child's attention while they learn. I think it's a great addition to the 22Learn family of educational apps, and I look forward to seeing more of its kind in the future.

As usual, this app from 22Learn is absolutely wonderful. I love them because, working with children everyday, I need apps that are fun AND educational. While this app may just seem like musical toys to a child, the impact of music is not to be understated. An interest in music now can lead a child to pursue musical interests later, such as playing instruments and vocal performance. Research has shown time and again how musical knowledge benefits one's ability to multitask, think critically, and perform fine motor actions. This app is a wonderful introduction to music for children. It is sure to spark their interest and perhaps they will want to learn more about instruments and other types of music.

The app itself is delightfully-fun and sure to be a hit with children. It is easy to navigate and buttons can be pressed accurately with little hands. The main screen displays buttons that, when pressed, start one of the 8 fun music activities. The first is 'Animal Piano'. In this activity, players use shape recognition to fill in pieces of the piano. Afterward, users can freely tap the keys to create music or tap one of the piano's icons to hear a song, such as the Alphabet Song. The keys light up as songs are played, so it IS possible to learn to tap them out on your own, though this is obviously complex for young learners. Players can also record and play back their own melodies which is absolutely amazing!

'Matching Sounds' requires matching sounds/colors. It is a fun activity and, again, users can freely tap sounds, record, and play upon completion. 'Xylophone' also requires color matching and 'Drums' asks the user to build drums by matching shapes and colors. I think 'Drums' is the highlight activity for many children- there is just something about drums that screams 'cool' and kids love to beat on them even in a virtual environment. As with the other activities, rhythms can be recorded and played back.

The last two activities are 'Music Machine' and 'Super Music Machine'. Music Machine is advanced because it shows actual notes on music staves which is just tremendous. This is by far my favorite activity. Players drag notes onto a disc in the order they wish them to be played. Empty spaces can be left to create pauses. The user hits 'play' and the machine loops the track over and over. Tempo (speed) can be adjusted as well. Super Music Machine involves three discs, allowing the user to work with the note tones, xylophone tones, and drum beats. It's absolutely remarkable detail for a young learners app.

If your child loves musical toys at all, or even just songs in general, they will love this app. It has unlimited play potential due to its freestyle nature. It is very intuitive to use and the help button is great. It actually shows a virtual hand on the screen that displays what to do- absolutely perfect for children playing on their own. When you consider the cute animals, professional voice acting, and attractive illustrations, you have the perfect symphony of fun activities that is Animal Piano!

I have the paid version of this app and absolutely love and recommend it- kids really eat it up! The value of the paid app is way more than the low price implies and potential re-playability is endless! It's a great way for young learners to explore an interest in music. Musical ability has been linked to higher test scores and better school performance. This is due to the need to multitask, read notes, and perform physical actions at the same time. Musical play strengthens the brain and can be very beneficial for learners.

The free version only includes animal piano unlocked. I do wish it included one additional activity to give a better feel for the app's variation. The activities are all unique, so the value here is wonderful. Animal piano is a great introduction regardless. Users match the piano shapes and can play full songs or tap around the keys once finished. Users can also record and play back their own melodies. The activities mostly include the record/playback capability, which is awesome. Matching Sounds is similar as users must match note tones and colors. Users can then tap around and make their own melodies. Xylophone also utilizes color matching, and Drums uses color and shape recognition in addition to the sound effects. Children will love creating their own xylophone and drum melodies! If your child likes the piano activity, they will surely love the entire app as it is similar.

In my opinion, Music Machine and Super Music Machine are the crown jewels of this activity suite. In music machine, notes are actually labeled and displayed on a music staff. Users can drag the notes onto a disc and press play to have the melody on the disc played. Speed (tempo) can be adjusted, and pauses (rests) can be created by leaving empty spots in the disc. Super Music Machine is the same, but adds the xylophone and drum discs in addition to the note tone disc. These are great activities for those that desire a little more 'depth'. They can be used to teach your child a little about notes and how music is read, as well as music terminology (a pause is a rest in music, speed is tempo, notes are written on a musical staff, etc.).

Overall, this is the best musical app I have found for children. Kids gravitate toward those musical toys, and this virtual version really hits the spot. Instead of one bulky, expensive xylophone toy they can only use at home, they can use this virtual alternative to create their own masterpieces! Limitless value for a low price- that is this app! The professional voice acting and illustrations include cute animals that are sure to please. Try it out and upgrade if your child likes the piano- it is totally worth it JUST for the music machine!

Abby Monkey is back, and this time she's brought her magic laptop! For those unfamiliar with Abby Monkey, she is a cute, friendly character that young children really love. This app is very much geared toward preschool learning, as it covers the basics (shapes, colors, numbers, common objects, etc.).

I use a lot of 22Learn apps as I work as a tutor and babysitter, and I recently purchased the Abby Monkey Magic Laptop for Preschool app as an activity for my young niece who I babysit. She will be starting preschool this upcoming year, and I thought this was just perfect for some educational playtime. The app reminds me of one of those talking phone toys most young children have, and even the youngest kids like to feel like they have their own 'technology'. The app is basically a board of buttons that children can press to their heart's content and learn from voice commands in the process.

The top half of the 'laptop' features a menu board of topics. Farm animals, toys, colors, zoo animals, vehicles, instruments, numbers 1-10 and then 11-20, alphabet, fruits, vegetables, and shapes are included. This is a pretty nice spread that seems to align well with what preschool children learn about in school. The top half also includes the ability to switch between the two functions- play mode and learning mode. A 'screen' area in the center displays information and pictures when the buttons are tapped.

The bottom half features all the objects in each category. For example, if you select colors, each of the 10 buttons will represent a different color. Pressing a button causes the app to say the name of the object, display an image of it, and play a related sound if possible (dogs will bark, trucks will go vroom, and colors will make various musical sounds). There are also buttons that say 'hello' and 'goodbye' in different tones and ways while displaying various faces. Other buttons play sounds and music. Images are full-color and beautifully illustrated, and the app features professional voiceovers which is a nice touch.

During play mode, users can simply tap around the app to learn the names of the objects and see pictures representing them. In learning mode, the app will ask users to find a specific object. Correct answers are rewarded with verbal praise, and incorrect answers will prompt the app to provide hints. Overall, I think it's a great app for kids, my niece loved it, and it includes every topic you could want covered in a basic learning app. It is definitely an app that needs to be enjoyed with the sound on, so it may not be great for on-the-go entertainment or when quiet is desired. Most children will enjoy pressing the many buttons and learning about their favorite things.

I work as a tutor and babysit often, so I have purchased and enjoyed many 22Learn apps. I believe they are a great value for their professional quality, and they are based on real educational methods. This comes in handy when I am looking for fun and inexpensive ways to interact with and teach my students. Many of my students have difficulty in math and wish to perform better on timed multiplication, addition, subtraction, or division tests. The best way to prepare is through 'skill and drill' exercises such as flashcards, but these can get stale fast.

22Learn approaches this problem with fun and inventive ways to drill math facts. I simply load the apps on my Android phone and carry it with me. Students have had no trouble using the apps with a bit of guidance. I recently purchased Winter Math Adventure and have since tested it with my students. My students range in age from grades 1-5, so this app was perfect due to being able to alter the difficulty and types of problems displayed (addition, multiplication, etc.). This means all my students can play with and use the app for a long time to come as they grow more skilled. They especially love seeing their scores recorded in the high scores section and trying to beat them.

This app is similar to the 22Learn Halloween Math title, but I love having a few themes to choose from. Once the app is opened and Santa's train tapped, a menu of game modes opens. Students can then select an avatar (there's snowmen, gingerbread men, penguins, etc.) and enter their names. Students can select the types of problems displayed and the difficulty at this screen. It's very simple and I often let the kids choose the difficulty they think is right after a few games are played, allowing them to gauge their skills.

This app includes five math games. In Catch a Star, a math problem is displayed and users have to tap the star that holds the correct answer. Penguin Craze is similar, but penguins hold the answers instead of stars. Winter Match displays math problems and answers on cards, and users must select the correct pairs. Snowman Hunter displays two snowballs with possible answers to a given math problem. I typically use this game as an 'easier' option, as there are less choices, but it helps students decide which answers are more reasonable (for example, if I have 10x20=? and one answer is 15 and the other is 120, which is more likely to be correct?). Math Bingo displays problems and a board of answers, encouraging students to form a 'bingo' with their correct selections.

The app runs pretty well on my HTC Android phone. I have had slight problems getting the entered student name to go through on the first try, but this is a moot issue. There's settings to adjust the time allotted for users to input answers for the timed games and the typical music and sound toggles. The app also tracks high scores which can be reset from this menu. I think the app looks nice, the professional voice effects are appreciated, and 22Learn apps have been a hit with my students. I would recommend this app to anyone looking for new ways to work on math facts.

The whole idea of the game is deceptively simple. You join the coloured dot to the other dot of the same color, but the tracks must not cross each other. It starts out with a nice slow gentle learning curve, but if you look at the games of the day, you can see how complicated it can get. For me, I found that the biggest help in solving the mid-range puzzles, was to look for two dots of the same color that can be connected by a track around the outer squares of the board, before trying to connect the other person the middle of the board. It does not always work that way, but it is the biggest help I have found. If you get in a mess, so not worry about restarting that level, you do not "lose a life" or anything like that. That along with no timed rounds, or limited moves rounds means the Flow Free games can be quite relaxing if you want, and is why I recommend them so heartily. Of course you can go for the timed rounds if you wish. Lots of choices in these logic puzzles are another clue that they are well designed.

Keep trying to beat each level until you do.  A totally satisfying game experience.  If we could give 10 stars I would.  I'm looking forward to your next game.......no pressure!

This game was interesting until I found a very obviously wrong problem. If one is wrong, then others are likely wrong, too. The "Water in the Wine" one is WRONG.

It asked: You have two glasses equally full of liquids. One has wine and the other has water. Take one spoonful of water and pour it into the wine and stir it up. Then, using the same spoon, take a spoonful of wine and pour it into the water glass and stir it up.

Now: Is there more water in the wine? More wine in the water? Or are they the same?

MY answer was there is more water in the wine (I figured they meant percentage), because once you mix the spoon of water into the wine you are diluting it, so that spoonful you transfer to the water has water in it, it's not 100% wine, like the first transfer was 100% water. MY answer is correct. Theirs is not. The fact that they screwed this up is just outrageous and the rest of the game is probably flawed as well.

This is exactly what I was looking for! I needed something to help my homeschooled kids learn and practice cursive without spending a fortune on workbooks. I figured out that I want them to learn the "DN" font, the main difference being the capital Q looks like a large 2 and that's what I learned in school.

One strange thing, though; the way it puts a "child lock" by asking for the solution to a simple math problem won't stop my kids since they know how to do those problems. Most kids in America learn cursive starting in 3rd grade and definitely can add 13+9 by then. :) My suggestion to the developer is to change it to a passcode instead.

The Train Schedule puzzle has two errors in it. First, there is a completely unnecessary clue (the second one, because that info was already deduced from the first clue!) and a name is typed "Malou" when it's actually Mary in another clue. I figured it out, luckily.

Next time, test the game yourself before publishing, developer..

I picked up the free version of the game and couldn't put it down.  The background graphics are amazing.  I even found myself staring at the backgrounds and forgetting to watch what I was supposed to be doing.  The game is a side scrolling game and you must keep up with the scrolling of the screen or you fail and must start that section over again.  The premise of the game is that you must control a bat-like creature while it flies, rolls and tumbles (mainly flies) through an absolutely unending array of creatively designed obstacles and pitfalls.  Many of the sections require split second timing and control of your character to complete.  The characters motion is controlled with either tapping or touching and holding a spot on the screen.  While the screen is being touched, your character moves forward/rolls/flies (and climbs in altitude while flying).  As soon as you stop touching the screen your character stops moving forward or starts dropping if it was flying.  Sometimes some very carefully timed and repetitive "taps" on the screen are what is required to get your character to fly and dodge and bob its way through to the next level.  There are number of power-up so to speak that do a number of things such as make your character smaller, larger, faster slower, stop the motion around it, slow down time, speed up time, etc.  If you simply cannot get through a particular area or "checkpoint" you do have the option to "skip" that checkpoint and be placed at the start of the next one.  I found that I could get through most of the areas without resorting to skipping them (but admittedly not all)  but many required that I repeat the area over and over again to get it just right.  Split second timing and control of your character (and speed) are essential in getting through many of the levels.  There were 40 or so levels in the free version.  As soon as I finished those I immediately purchased the paid version which you have the option to do through inside the game itself.  The paid version has a couple of options one of which is some sort of multiplayer mode.  I didn't try that one myself.  You get another 40 or so levels with the paid version.  My one and only complaint about the game is that there weren't even more levels.  The creativity in designing this game and the obstacles is just amazing.  I couldn't wait to see what sort of strange and bizarre things I'd have to get around/through on the next level.  I found myself saying again and again, "WHO comes up with this stuff...I love it!"  I hope to see even more levels or another game incorporating many of the same elements as in this one put out by the people that brought us Badland.  I think this was the easiest five star rating I've ever given.  Get the free version now while it's still free and get the paid version before it goes up in price.

The slots are fun to play but as is typical for so many apps today, you end up having to pay real money to continue after a very short while.
